issues.title: Add a sliver-compatible positioned list with scroll-to-index support
issues.body:
### Use case

### Use case

I need a variable-height alphabetical contact list that:

- Works inside CustomScrollView
- Can be combined with SliverAppBar
- Supports jumpToIndex and scrollToIndex
- Reports the currently visible item indexes
- Remains smooth when dragging an A–Z index rail

### Current limitation

ScrollablePositionedList supports index-based scrolling, but it is a complete
ScrollView and cannot be inserted into CustomScrollView as a sliver.

SliverList works with SliverAppBar, but ScrollController only accepts pixel
offsets and cannot reliably scroll to an index when children have variable
heights.


### Proposal

### Proposal

Provide an official sliver-compatible positioned-list API, potentially similar to:

SliverScrollablePositionedList.builder(...)

with:

- ItemScrollController
- ItemPositionsListener
- jumpTo(index: ...)
- scrollTo(index: ...)
- Variable-height child support

The exact API or widget name can follow Flutter framework conventions.

Refactor scrollable_semantics_test.dart to avoid shared top-level SemanticsTester
issues.body:
## What needs cleaning up

`packages/flutter/test/widgets/scrollable_semantics_test.dart` keeps a single `SemanticsTester` in a top-level variable that is reused across every test in the file:

```dart
void main() {
  late SemanticsTester semantics;
  ...
}
```

Sharing one tester across tests is fragile. If a test doesn't dispose of it (for example, when a test fails partway through), that state can leak into the next test and produce confusing, order-dependent failures.

## What to do

Refactor the file so each test owns its own `SemanticsTester` and disposes of it reliably. A `setUp`/`tearDown` pair, or `addTearDown` inside each test, both work well here. After the change there should be no shared top-level `SemanticsTester`.

## Scope

- Only `packages/flutter/test/widgets/scrollable_semantics_test.dart`.
- Test-only change; no framework behavior changes.
- All existing tests in the file should still pass.

## Context

Noticed during review of #188788. It was intentionally left out of that PR to keep it focused on the fix, and tracked here for a separate follow-up.

issues.title: No way to scale down only the text of a composite child to resolve overflow
issues.body:
## Use case

A widget that lays out a caller-supplied `Widget` child cannot resolve text overflow inside that child by making **only the text** smaller.

This is a granularity problem. The container is the only party that knows the available width; the text that needs to shrink is somewhere inside a subtree the container did not build and cannot address. The framework's only shrink-to-fit primitive, `FittedBox`, operates on the whole subtree and scales it geometrically, so it cannot express "shrink the text, leave everything else alone".

### Concrete case

A design-system button whose label is a `Widget`, so callers can pass a `Text`, a
`Text.rich`, or a composite:

```dart
MyButton(
  label: Row(
    mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
    children: [
      const Icon(Icons.bolt),
      Text(l10n.placeBid),   // ← this is what must shrink
      const CountBadge(3),
    ],
  ),
)
```

The app is localised into 17 locales with machine-translated copy, so this label overflows in locales nobody tested. The desired behaviour is the obvious one: the `Text` renders at the largest type step that fits, the icon and the badge keep their sizes, and the `Row` re-flows normally.

That is not expressible today.

### What the framework offers, and why each option fails

#### `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)`

This is the only shrink-to-fit primitive. It applies a geometric transform to the entire child, so:

- the icon and the badge shrink along with the text, as though the label were a zoomed-out screenshot rather than a laid-out subtree;
- spacing, padding, and border widths scale too, taking the result off the design system's grid, and glyphs land on a transformed, non-integral font size rather than a real type step;
- the child is laid out with unbounded constraints (`RenderFittedBox.performLayout` passes `const BoxConstraints()`, `rendering/proxy_box.dart`), so composite children that need a bounded width fail outright.

#### Reaching the `Text` through inherited data

`DefaultTextStyle` is the only channel that can influence a `Text` the container did not build, and it is the semantically correct one: text that did not specify its own `fontSize` participates, an `Icon` is naturally immune because it sizes from `IconTheme`, and a badge with an explicit style is immune because `Text` merges its own style over the inherited one.

But the font size must be chosen at **build** time, while the value that would make it fit is only knowable after **layout**. The container therefore cannot compute it.

#### Owning the text

Taking a `String` instead of a `Widget` makes the policy possible, but then composite children are impossible, which is the whole point of the slot.

We can give alternative constructors (`MyButton.text`), which is what we are doing today, but doing so makes the API unnecessarily complex.

We could also make a `MyText` widget that implements this behavior, but then we are diverging from the upstream's `Text` implementation and will have extra burden to maintain this custom widget.

### Why this is blocked, mechanically

There are two independent walls:

1. **No primitive scales typography rather than geometry.** `FittedBox` transforms a rendered subtree; nothing re-shapes text at a smaller size. So any shrinking necessarily applies to everything, uniformly.
2. **The only channel into an unowned `Text` is build-time, and the answer is layout-time.** `DefaultTextStyle` propagation is exactly the right mechanism, but its value must be fixed before the layout that would determine it.

It's worth noting that the underlying capability already exists one layer down, and is simply not reachable from outside: `RenderParagraph` owns a `TextPainter`, assigning `TextPainter.text` calls `markNeedsLayout()`, and `layout()` rebuilds the `ui.Paragraph` from a fresh `ParagraphStyle`. Re-shaping text at a different size inside `performLayout` is already legal and cheap for short strings — it is what `auto_size_text` does one layer up. What is missing is any way for a container, or an ancestor, to ask for it.

### Where else this bites

- Any design-system component with a size contract and a `Widget` slot: buttons, chips, tabs, app-bar titles, list tiles, table cells.
- Localisation generally. Space reserved in the design language cannot be guaranteed in every locale, and today a container's only ways to degrade are truncating the text or squashing the whole composite.
- Accessibility. When a user raises the system text scale, a fixed-height container needs to scale back the text specifically — not the icons and not the padding.

## Proposal

Provide a way for text to be scaled down to fit the space its container gives it, when the container does not own the `Text` widget without scaling its siblings.

I am asking for the capability rather than a particular API. Several shapes would satisfy it; these are some suggestions (probably the most obvious ones):

1. **An extensible overflow policy.** Make `TextOverflow` an open type consulted by `RenderParagraph.performLayout` (given the constraints, the span, and a `measure(TextStyle)` closure) rather than a closed enum. Because `Text.overflow already falls back to `DefaultTextStyle.overflow`, an ancestor could then set the policy for a subtree it did not build. This shape also happens to unlock custom truncation markers, middle/start truncation, and reporting that text was truncated — all currently impossible for the same reason.
2. **An inheritable "text fit" policy separate from `TextOverflow`** — e.g. a `TextFit` inherited widget that `RenderParagraph` consults during layout, leaving the existing overflow enum untouched.

### Costs I would expect maintainers to weigh

- Any policy that re-shapes text pays extra shaping, whereas `TextOverflow`'s current modes are either engine-side within the same pass (`ellipsis`, via `ParagraphStyle.ellipsis`) or paint-time (`fade`, `clip`). That is presumably why the enum is closed, and it is a legitimate objection. It could be mitigated by consulting a policy only when the text actually overflows, and keeping the four built-ins on their present paths.
- Selection geometry, `didExceedMaxLines`, and semantics would need defined behavior for a policy that restyles rather than truncates.

issues.title: Proposal:Framework redoes cacheable work on hot paint/build paths (BoxDecoration shadows, InheritedModel.inheritFrom)
issues.body:
### Use case

While profiling release builds on iOS/Android I found spots where the framework redoes cacheable work on hot paths:

1. **`_BoxDecorationPainter._paintShadows`** (`painting/box_decoration.dart`) calls `BoxShadow.toPaint()` (a new `Paint` + native `MaskFilter`) for every shadow on every paint, even though the decoration is immutable and the painter is retained across frames. `_ShapeDecorationPainter` already caches these in `_shadowPaints`.

2. **`InheritedModel.inheritFrom`** (`widgets/inherited_model.dart`) allocates a `List` and recursively walks ancestors on every aspect lookup. Nothing in the framework overrides `isSupportedAspect` (it defaults to true), so the walk virtually always terminates at the nearest model. This is the path behind `MediaQuery.sizeOf` and friends, which run on nearly every widget build; `Text.build` alone goes through it five times per build.

A third, Cupertino-specific item (`_CupertinoEdgeShadowPainter` allocating ~20 `Paint`s per transition frame) was split into #190198 as requested, so it can be routed to the owning team independently.

### Proposal

Each has a small, behavior-preserving fix following patterns that already exist in the codebase:

1. Cache the shadow `Paint`s the same way `_ShapeDecorationPainter` does.
2. Add a fast path that depends on the nearest model directly when it supports the aspect (identical dependencies to the list-based walk), falling back to the existing walk otherwise.

PRs: #190194 (item 1), #190189 (item 2).

issues.title: Add ability to disable entire Form
issues.body:
### Use case

Nearly every app has forms. Some has tons of forms. And nearly all of these apps need to disable the whole form under some conditions.
For example, a profile page can be a form and it should be disabled after registration, then become enabled after "Edit" button press and so on. A huge KYC forms on the operator side of the products need the same logic.
As of now, Flutter's `FormState` class lacks this functionality. To add it we have to create our own implementation of a `Form` + `FormState` and wrappers for all the `FormField`s we use, so that they can pass `MyForm.maybeOf(context).enabled ?? true` to Flutter's `TextFormField` and others.
That kind of lacking functionalities in Form API is the reason there are so many form-packages like `reactive_forms`, `flutter_form_builder` and others, the reason every team/project has it's own form approach, the reason there's no **standard** known to everyone. It increases the threshold for entry into the projects, which results in high costs on a global scale.

### Proposal

1. Add a new `bool enabled` property to the `Form` class (`true` by default);
2. Make `FormField.enabled` property nullable (and `null` - the default value);
3. Use `widget.enabled ?? Form.maybeOf(context).enabled ?? true` inside the `FormFieldState`.

This way we can disable the whole forms, while still being able to enable some concrete fields if required

issues.title: Minimize cross imports in examples
issues.body:
The examples, located [in the package root](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/master/examples) and [in packages/flutter](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/master/packages/flutter/examples), should avoid cross imports. 

  * If an example is unrelated to Material and Cupertino, consider refactoring it to only use Widgets.
  * If an example is realted to Material or Cupertino, consider moving it to material_ui or cupertino_ui.

See [knownExamplesCrossImports](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/dev/bots/check_examples_cross_imports.dart#L117), which contains a list of all example files with cross imports.  The examples in [api/lib/material](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/master/packages/flutter/examples/api/lib/material) and [api/lib/cupertino](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/tree/master/packages/flutter/examples/api/lib/cupertino) do not need to be migrated because they have already been moved to material_ui or cupertino_ui.

As discussed in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/190237#discussion_r3684846579, there's a small amount of concern for these imports of material_ui and cupertino_ui causing complicated migrations.

Part of https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/177028

issues.title: Support Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) with non-monotonic frame timestamps and resilient animations
issues.body:
## Background Modern displays across all major operating systems (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux) support **Variable Refresh Rate (VRR)** / **Adaptive Refresh Rate** / **ProMotion**, dynamically adjusting their refresh rates on the fly rather than running at a fixed cadence. * **Mobile devices** drop refresh rates significantly (e.g., down to 1 Hz or 10 Hz) when screen content is static to conserve battery. * **Desktop devices** dynamically pace refresh rates to match render output and prevent screen tearing. Historically, VRR has caused issues in the Flutter framework when presentation timestamps appear to "travel backwards in time," triggering asserts in `AnimationController` (such as `elapsedInSeconds >= 0.0` in `_tick()`) and crashing debug sessions: * [#106277](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/106277#issuecomment-3165226889) * [#190289](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190289#issuecomment-5145345685) * [flutter-team-archive/engine#55310](https://github.com/flutter-team-archive/engine/pull/55310) (2024 Engine commit mitigating time-traveling frames via clamping) ## Problem: "Time-Traveling" Presentation Timestamps When an OS paces frames at a very low refresh rate (e.g., 1 Hz), Flutter may be asked to render the next frame with a presentation timestamp far in the future (`t + 1000ms`). During that 1000 ms gap, if the system state changes (e.g., user interaction, incoming animation trigger), the OS may decide it needs an immediate **interstitial frame** and invoke a callback with a timestamp *sooner* than the previously scheduled frame (`t + 33ms`). *Note*: @jtmcdole believes in most cases the operating system will still retain the original `t + 1000ms` frame and present it after any interstitial frames are generated; though that's up to the operating system. ### Evolution of Handling Non-Monotonic Frame Times | Era | Behavior | Limitation / Impact | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Prior to flutter-team-archive/engine#55310** | The Engine passed raw OS presentation timestamps directly to the Framework. | • **Debug builds:** Crashed due to monotonicity asserts (`elapsedInSeconds >= 0.0`) in `AnimationController._tick()`.
• **Release builds:** Rendered without asserts, but could cause glitches in time-dependent animations. | | **Today** | The Engine prevents time from traveling backwards by **clamping** presentation timestamps. | • Several consecutive frames can be delivered to the Framework with the **exact same timestamp**.
• Destroys delta-time accuracy (`Δt = 0`), breaking physics simulations and pacing calculations. | ## Proposed Solution Instead of modifying frame timestamps in the Engine, Flutter should pass accurate presentation timestamps to the Framework and make animation handling resilient to non-monotonic time. * [ ] Remove monotonicity asserts: Remove or relax time-progression asserts in `_tick()` (`elapsedInSeconds >= 0.0`) where appropriate. * [ ] Stop clamping presentation timestamps: Allow non-monotonic presentation timestamps to pass from the Engine to the Framework so frame timing reflects actual OS scheduling. * [ ] Support Declarative (Idempotent) Animations: Establish patterns and framework support for stateless, function-of-time animations (`𝑓(t)`) that are mathematically idempotent and inherently immune to time moving backwards or out of order. * [ ] Support Stateful / Accumulation Animations: Build explicit safeguards into step-based or accumulation-based animations (e.g., physics simulations, particle systems, completed animations) so they handle non-monotonic timestamps or negative delta times gracefully without breaking state. * [ ] Document VRR / ProMotion interactions with the Flutter frame pipeline, offering guidance on choosing between declarative and simulation animations for custom tickers and controllers.

Proposal: Animation listener notification copies the listener list even when there are no listeners
issues.body:
### Use case

Continuing the profiling from #190187, `notifyListeners` and `notifyStatusListeners` in `animation/listener_helpers.dart` copy the listener collection on every notification:

```dart
final List<VoidCallback> localListeners = _listeners.toList(growable: false);
```

The copy exists so listeners can be added or removed while the callbacks run, which is necessary — but it happens unconditionally, including for the many animations that have no listeners of that kind. An `AnimationController` that only has a status listener still allocates a list for its value listeners on every tick, and vice versa. With several controllers running, that is a handful of allocations per frame that produce nothing.

`toList` also goes through `Iterable.length`, whose default implementation walks the whole collection with an iterator, even though `ObserverList` and `HashedObserverList` both wrap something that knows its own length.

### Proposal

Return early from both methods when the collection is empty, and override `length` on `ObserverList` and `HashedObserverList`.

Measured with an AOT microbenchmark (median of 5 runs of 2M iterations, macOS arm64 / Pixel 9 / iPhone):

| | macOS | Pixel 9 | iPhone |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notifyListeners`, no listeners | 20.7 -> 4.3ns | 34.3 -> 6.9ns | -78% |
| `notifyStatusListeners`, no listeners | 11.3 -> 4.0ns | 17.5 -> 6.2ns | -61% |
| `ObserverList.length` (10 entries) | 33.9 -> 1.3ns | 70.9 -> 3.8ns | -95% |
| `HashedObserverList.length` (10 entries) | 44.0 -> 3.3ns | 82.2 -> 6.2ns | -91% |

Notification with listeners present is unchanged (within noise on all three).

[Android] HCPP: PlatformViewsController2.onEndFrame() aborts the process when it runs after the FlutterView detaches
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Reproducible app: https://github.com/amaan-0331/hcpp-onendframe-crash-repro

Requires Android 14+ (API 34) and a Vulkan-capable device or emulator. HCPP silently no-ops on the
Impeller OpenGLES backend, so the repro sets `io.flutter.embedding.android.ImpellerBackend` to
`vulkan` alongside `EnableHcpp`.

1. `flutter run` the repro app. Confirm it shows "HCPP supported: true" and a blue native view.
2. Press back to finish the activity.
3. Launch the app again, wait for the native view to render, and press back again.

Or run `./repro.sh`, which drives the same loop and reports aborts.

The app registers a trivial Kotlin `PlatformView` (a `TextView`), creates it with
`PlatformViewsService.initHybridAndroidView`, and caches the `FlutterEngine` in
`Application.onCreate` so the engine outlives the activity. No third-party plugins are involved.


### Expected results

Destroying the activity while an HCPP platform view is on screen tears down cleanly.

### Actual results

The process aborts. Every teardown where the platform view had rendered crashes — 5 aborts in 10
iterations of the loop above, which is every warm teardown (each abort kills the process, so the
following launch is a cold start with no platform view yet, and does not crash).

`PlatformViewsController2.onEndFrame()` dereferences the result of `getRootSurfaceControl()` with no
null check:

```java
// PlatformViewsController2.java:669
@RequiresApi(API_LEVELS.API_34)
public void onEndFrame() {
  SurfaceControl.Transaction tx = new SurfaceControl.Transaction();
  for (int i = 0; i < activeTransactions.size(); i++) {
    tx = tx.merge(activeTransactions.get(i));
  }
  activeTransactions.clear();
  flutterView.invalidate();
  flutterView.getRootSurfaceControl().applyTransactionOnDraw(tx);   // <-- NPE
}
```

`AndroidExternalViewEmbedder2::SubmitFlutterView` posts `onEndFrame2()` from the raster thread to the
platform thread on every frame, including frames with no platform layers
(`external_view_embedder_2.cc:73-91` and `:168-203`). By the time that task runs on the main looper
the `FlutterView` may no longer be attached to a window, and `View.getRootSurfaceControl()` is
documented to return null in that case. `flutterView` itself can also be null, since
`detachFromView()` (`:269`) nulls it without any corresponding guard here.

The resulting exception is not merely logged — the JNI caller ends with
`FML_CHECK(fml::jni::CheckException(env))` (`platform_view_android_jni_impl.cc:2370`), which turns
any pending Java exception into `abort()`. There is no Dart-side recovery and no application-level
workaround other than not enabling HCPP.

Two related paths that this repro does not exercise:

- `createOverlaySurface()` (`:716`) dereferences `flutterView.getRootSurfaceControl()` the same way.
- `FlutterJNI.endFrame2()` (`:1379`) throws `RuntimeException` when `platformViewsController2` is
  null, which reaches the same `FML_CHECK`.

This was originally reported from the field on a Xiaomi HyperOS 3 (Android 16) device running a
released app, with an identical abort signature. That app does not use a cached engine; the cached
engine in the repro makes the same race deterministic by keeping `FlutterJNI` attached across the
activity destroy. The equivalent window exists in an ordinary teardown, where
`detachFromFlutterEngine()` runs before the engine is destroyed, which would explain why it appears
in the field as a rare crash.


### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

Full app: https://github.com/amaan-0331/hcpp-onendframe-crash-repro

`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`:

```xml
<meta-data android:name="io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableHcpp" android:value="true" />
<meta-data android:name="io.flutter.embedding.android.ImpellerBackend" android:value="vulkan" />
```

`lib/main.dart` (platform view creation):

```dart
PlatformViewLink(
  viewType: 'hcpp_repro/box',
  surfaceFactory: (BuildContext context, PlatformViewController controller) {
    return AndroidViewSurface(
      controller: controller as AndroidViewController,
      gestureRecognizers: const <Factory<OneSequenceGestureRecognizer>>{},
      hitTestBehavior: PlatformViewHitTestBehavior.opaque,
    );
  },
  onCreatePlatformView: (PlatformViewCreationParams params) {
    return PlatformViewsService.initHybridAndroidView(
        id: params.id,
        viewType: params.viewType,
        layoutDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
        creationParamsCodec: const StandardMessageCodec(),
        onFocus: () => params.onFocusChanged(true),
      )
      ..addOnPlatformViewCreatedListener(params.onPlatformViewCreated)
      ..create();
  },
)
```

`MainActivity` uses a cached engine created in `Application.onCreate`, so it outlives the activity:

```kotlin
class MainActivity : FlutterActivity() {
    override fun getCachedEngineId(): String = ENGINE_ID
    override fun shouldDestroyEngineWithHost(): Boolean = false
}
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

[Upload media here]

</details>


### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/fml/platform/android/jni_util.cc(206)] java.lang.NullPointerException: Attempt to invoke interface method 'boolean android.view.AttachedSurfaceControl.applyTransactionOnDraw(android.view.SurfaceControl$Transaction)' on a null object reference
E flutter : 	at io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformViewsController2.onEndFrame(PlatformViewsController2.java:676)
E flutter : 	at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.endFrame2(FlutterJNI.java:1379)
E flutter : 	at android.os.MessageQueue.nativePollOnce(Native Method)
E flutter : 	at android.os.MessageQueue.nextLegacy(MessageQueue.java:913)
E flutter : 	at android.os.MessageQueue.next(MessageQueue.java:1025)
E flutter : 	at android.os.Looper.loopOnce(Looper.java:196)
E flutter : 	at android.os.Looper.loop(Looper.java:338)
E flutter : 	at android.app.ActivityThread.main(ActivityThread.java:9067)

F libc    : Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), code -1 (SI_QUEUE) in tid 15144 (hcpp.hcpp_repro), pid 15144 (hcpp.hcpp_repro)
```

```java
}
```

`AndroidExternalViewEmbedder2::SubmitFlutterView` posts `onEndFrame2()` from the raster thread to the
platform thread on every frame, including frames with no platform layers
(`external_view_embedder_2.cc:73-91` and `:168-203`). By the time that task runs on the main looper
the `FlutterView` may no longer be attached to a window, and `View.getRootSurfaceControl()` is
documented to return null in that case. `flutterView` itself can also be null, since
`detachFromView()` (`:269`) nulls it without any corresponding guard here.

The resulting exception is not merely logged — the JNI caller ends with
`FML_CHECK(fml::jni::CheckException(env))` (`platform_view_android_jni_impl.cc:2370`), which turns
any pending Java exception into `abort()`. There is no Dart-side recovery and no application-level
workaround other than not enabling HCPP.

Two related paths that this repro does not exercise:

- `createOverlaySurface()` (`:716`) dereferences `flutterView.getRootSurfaceControl()` the same way.
- `FlutterJNI.endFrame2()` (`:1379`) throws `RuntimeException` when `platformViewsController2` is
  null, which reaches the same `FML_CHECK`.

This was originally reported from the field on a Xiaomi HyperOS 3 (Android 16) device running a
released app, with an identical abort signature. That app does not use a cached engine; the cached
engine in the repro makes the same race deterministic by keeping `FlutterJNI` attached across the
activity destroy. The equivalent window exists in an ordinary teardown, where
`detachFromFlutterEngine()` runs before the engine is destroyed, which would explain why it appears
in the field as a rare crash.

[Android][Accessibility] AccessibilityBridge$Api31Impl.isBoldText still throws NoSuchFieldError for fontWeightAdjustment on 3.44.8
issues.body:
#184286 was closed by #184630, and I cherry-picked it to the 3.44 branch in #189759, which shipped in stable 3.44.8. The crash still reaches production on 3.44.8. The previous thread is locked, so I am opening this as a new report.

## What happens

`AccessibilityBridge` is constructed during `FlutterActivity.onCreate`. Its constructor calls `setBoldTextFlag()` behind `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= API_LEVELS.API_31`, and `setBoldTextFlag()` reads the field through the `Api31Impl` helper:

```java
// AccessibilityBridge.java:663
boolean shouldBold =
    Api31Impl.isBoldText(rootAccessibilityView.getResources().getConfiguration());

// AccessibilityBridge.java:3267
private static class Api31Impl {
  @DoNotInline
  static boolean isBoldText(Configuration configuration) {
    int fontWeightAdjustment = configuration.fontWeightAdjustment;
    return fontWeightAdjustment != Configuration.FONT_WEIGHT_ADJUSTMENT_UNDEFINED
        && fontWeightAdjustment >= BOLD_TEXT_WEIGHT_ADJUSTMENT;
  }
}
```

Moving the read into `Api31Impl` stops the class verifier from resolving the field while `AccessibilityBridge` is loaded. It does not stop the read itself. On a ROM that reports `SDK_INT >= 31` while `android.content.res.Configuration` carries no `fontWeightAdjustment`, the guard passes, `isBoldText` is entered, and resolution fails there instead. The failure moved one frame down rather than going away.

## Stack trace (production, built with 3.44.8)

```
java.lang.NoSuchFieldError: No instance field fontWeightAdjustment of type I in class Landroid/content/res/Configuration; or its superclasses (declaration of 'android.content.res.Configuration' appears in /system/framework/framework.jar)
  at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge$Api31Impl.isBoldText (AccessibilityBridge.java)
  at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.setBoldTextFlag (AccessibilityBridge.java:663)
  at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init> (AccessibilityBridge.java:528)
  at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init> (AccessibilityBridge.java:463)
  at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterView.attachToFlutterEngine (FlutterView.java:1225)
  at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivityAndFragmentDelegate.onCreateView (FlutterActivityAndFragmentDelegate.java:437)
  at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivity.createFlutterView (FlutterActivity.java:802)
  at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivity.onCreate (FlutterActivity.java:652)
  at android.app.Activity.performCreate (Activity.java:7994)
  at android.app.Instrumentation.callActivityOnCreate (Instrumentation.java:1548)
  at android.app.ActivityThread.performLaunchActivity (ActivityThread.java:3406)
```

`Api31Impl` appearing in the frame confirms the build carries the 3.44.8 fix.

## Occurrences

Crashlytics, two releases of the same app, both built with 3.44.8:

- 2026-08-01: 10 events from 2 installations
- 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-07: 14 events from 4 installations

Every event reports `OnePlus8Pro` on Android 11, with the OS name unresolved. Architecture is `X86_64` in the August 1 batch and `ARM64` afterwards. Reported memory and storage are roughly 4.3 GB each, which does not match the retail device, so these are most likely automated environments rather than end users. The code path is the same either way: `FlutterActivity.onCreate` is the first frame, and the process dies before anything is drawn.

## Reproduction

I have no access to hardware, or to an image, that reports `SDK_INT >= 31` without the field, so I cannot supply a minimal reproduction. The condition is reproducible in principle with any `Configuration` that declares API 31 while omitting `fontWeightAdjustment`.

## Direction

On these ROMs the API level is not a reliable signal for the presence of the field, so gating on it cannot close the path. Containing the read so the flag falls back to "not bold" would leave startup intact. If that direction is acceptable, I can prepare the change.

[camera_android_camerax] Preview rotation is wrong on foldable inner (naturally-landscape) displays — `ImageReaderRotatedPreview` mixes display-rotation and device-orientation frames
issues.body:
## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Device | Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 (SM-F971N), Android 16, targetSdk 36 |
| Flutter | 3.44.8 (stable) |
| camera | 0.11.3 **and** 0.12.0+2 (both reproduce; upgrading changed nothing) |
| camera_android_camerax | 0.6.24+1 **and** 0.7.3 (both reproduce) |
| Rendering | Impeller (default). `surfaceProducerHandlesCropAndRotation() == false` → `ImageReaderRotatedPreview` path |
| App orientation | `SystemChrome.setPreferredOrientations([DeviceOrientation.portraitUp])`; on this display Android 16 ignores the restriction (sw ≥ 600dp), so the window rotates freely |

Related: #164493, #149177 (naturally-landscape devices — closed, but the ImageReader path regresses on foldables), #156974 (front preview flipped post ImageReader updates — same mirroring code region), #180499 (CameraPreview stretch under tight constraints), #168938 (rotation jank / nested RotatedBoxes). Searched for existing foldable reports: only #143516 (camera_web enumeration on Fold 5) exists; this appears to be the first report of the rotation defect on foldable inner displays.

## Summary

On the unfolded inner display (natural orientation: **landscape**):

- **Front camera preview is rotated 180° in every grip** (portraitUp / landscapeLeft / portraitDown / landscapeRight — all four measured). It is a rotation, not a mirror flip.
- **Back camera preview appears stretched** when the window is landscape (portrait-oriented content laid out in a landscape `AspectRatio` box).
- On the folded cover display (natural orientation: portrait) everything is correct.
- ML Kit face detection driven from the image stream fails in 3 of 4 grips for the same underlying reason (rotation hint no longer matches buffer content).

Locking the capture orientation (`lockCaptureOrientation(portraitUp)`) while the window is actually portrait fixes the folded/phone case, but is not applicable unfolded, where the window legitimately rotates.

## How we measured (method reproducible from any app)

We instrumented the app to walk the Element tree under the preview each frame and record every `RotatedBox.quarterTurns` between our widget and the `Texture`, i.e. the **actually applied** rotation chain:

```
CameraPreview               → RotatedBox(A)   (from deviceOrientation, camera_preview.dart)
ImageReaderRotatedPreview   → RotatedBox(B)   (computed in _computeRotationDegrees)
net = A + B (mod 4)
```

We also logged `CameraValue.deviceOrientation`, `previewSize`, `sensorOrientation`, lens facing, and the Flutter window size per sample.

## Measurements

### Front camera, `sensorOrientation: 270`, `previewSize: 320x240`

| State | deviceOrientation | A (CameraPreview) | B (ImageReader) | net | Visually |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Folded (portrait-natural display) | portraitUp | 0 | **3** | 270° | ✅ correct |
| **Unfolded** | portraitUp | 0 | **0** | 0° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | landscapeLeft | 3 | **0** | 270° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | portraitDown | 2 | **0** | 180° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | landscapeRight | 1 | **0** | 90° | ❌ 180° off |

The same physical grip that produces `B = 3` folded produces `B = 0` unfolded. The user-visible error is a **constant 180° in all four grips**.

### Back camera, `sensorOrientation: 90`, `previewSize: 720x480`

| State | deviceOrientation | A | B | net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Folded | portraitUp | 0 | 1 | 90° |
| Unfolded | portraitUp | 0 | 1 | 90° |
| Unfolded | landscapeLeft | 3 | −2 | 90° |
| Unfolded | portraitDown | 2 | 0 | **180°** |

With the window landscape, the net-90°-rotated (portrait-oriented) content sits in `CameraPreview`'s landscape `AspectRatio` box (`_isLandscape()` is true because `deviceOrientation` is landscape) → visible horizontal stretch. Box axis and content axis come from different frames.

## Analysis — the math is right, the frames are mixed

`ImageReaderRotatedPreview._computeRotationDegrees` (0.7.3):

```dart
double rotationDegrees =
    (sensorOrientationDegrees - currentDefaultDisplayRotationDegrees * sign + 360) % 360;
final double extraRotationDegrees =
    getPreAppliedQuarterTurnsRotationFromDeviceOrientation(orientation) * 90;
rotationDegrees -= extraRotationDegrees;
```

Fitting the measured values, the applied rotation matches this formula **exactly, with zero error in every sample**, given the display rotation values of a naturally-landscape display (window-portrait ⇔ `Surface.ROTATION_90`). The computation is internally consistent. The defect is that two inputs live in different reference frames:

- `currentDefaultDisplayRotationDegrees` — relative to the **display's natural orientation** (landscape on the unfolded panel);
- `getPreAppliedQuarterTurnsRotationFromDeviceOrientation(orientation)` and `sensorOrientationDegrees` — effectively relative to the **portrait chassis frame** (the frame in which the values are correct on the folded display).

On natural-portrait displays the two frames coincide and the formula works. On the unfolded panel they differ by one quarter turn, and the sum

```
ccw(displayRotation) + cw(preApplied(deviceOrientation))  (mod 4)
```

is **0 in every folded/phone sample and constantly 3 in every unfolded sample** across all grips — a clean signature of a frame mismatch rather than a race.

An additional consequence: the front-camera mirroring axis is chosen from `deviceOrientation` (`Transform.scale(scaleY/scaleX: -1)`, lines 151–158). A mirror about the wrong axis equals the correct mirror composed with a 180° rotation, which is exactly what users report ("rotated 180°, not flipped"), and why the error reads as 180° rather than 90°.

## Camera enumeration is fold-invariant (so apps cannot work around it by selection)

`availableCameras()` returns, byte-identical whether folded or unfolded:

```
0: back  sensorOrientation 90
1: front sensorOrientation 270
2: back  sensorOrientation 90
3: front sensorOrientation 270
```

Opening id 1 shows the user's face both folded and unfolded — physically different sensors (cover vs inner camera) behind one logical id, while the advertised `sensorOrientation` never changes. There is no signal an app could use to select differently.

## What we ruled out

- **Plugin upgrade** 0.6.24+1 → 0.7.3 (includes CameraX 1.6.0 and the 0.6.29 lens-direction change): byte-identical rotation chains before/after.
- **Stale enumeration caching in the app**: removed; enumeration verified fresh per session; fold-invariant regardless.
- **App-side geometry**: reproduced with `CameraPreview` used bare (no external constraints), so #180499-style tight-constraint stretching is an additional symptom, not the cause.

## Expected

`ImageReaderRotatedPreview` should compute the correction in a single frame — either by converting `Display.getRotation()` into the same frame as `DeviceOrientation`/`sensorOrientation` using the display's natural orientation, or by deriving the correction purely from the `deviceOrientation` stream as the SurfaceTexture path effectively does. The mirroring axis should be chosen in the same frame.

## Actual

Preview rotated 180° (front) / axis-mismatched stretch (back) on foldable inner displays; correct on the cover display and on regular phones.

## Repro

1. Any Flutter app with `CameraPreview`, portrait-locked via `setPreferredOrientations`, targetSdk 36.
2. Run on a foldable whose inner display is naturally landscape (measured here: Z Fold 8; sw unfolded 704dp → orientation restriction ignored by Android 16).
3. Unfold, open the front camera. Preview is rotated 180° in every grip; folding restores correctness.

- ML Kit face detection driven from the image stream fails in 3 of 4 grips for the same underlying reason (rotation hint no longer matches buffer content).

Locking the capture orientation (`lockCaptureOrientation(portraitUp)`) while the window is actually portrait fixes the folded/phone case, but is not applicable unfolded, where the window legitimately rotates.

## How we measured (method reproducible from any app)

We instrumented the app to walk the Element tree under the preview each frame and record every `RotatedBox.quarterTurns` between our widget and the `Texture`, i.e. the **actually applied** rotation chain:

```
CameraPreview               → RotatedBox(A)   (from deviceOrientation, camera_preview.dart)
ImageReaderRotatedPreview   → RotatedBox(B)   (computed in _computeRotationDegrees)
net = A + B (mod 4)
```

We also logged `CameraValue.deviceOrientation`, `previewSize`, `sensorOrientation`, lens facing, and the Flutter window size per sample.

## Measurements

### Front camera, `sensorOrientation: 270`, `previewSize: 320x240`

| State | deviceOrientation | A (CameraPreview) | B (ImageReader) | net | Visually |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Folded (portrait-natural display) | portraitUp | 0 | **3** | 270° | ✅ correct |
| **Unfolded** | portraitUp | 0 | **0** | 0° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | landscapeLeft | 3 | **0** | 270° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | portraitDown | 2 | **0** | 180° | ❌ 180° off |
| Unfolded | landscapeRight | 1 | **0** | 90° | ❌ 180° off |

The same physical grip that produces `B = 3` folded produces `B = 0` unfolded. The user-visible error is a **constant 180° in all four grips**.

### Back camera, `sensorOrientation: 90`, `previewSize: 720x480`

| State | deviceOrientation | A | B | net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Folded | portraitUp | 0 | 1 | 90° |
| Unfolded | portraitUp | 0 | 1 | 90° |
| Unfolded | landscapeLeft | 3 | −2 | 90° |
| Unfolded | portraitDown | 2 | 0 | **180°** |

With the window landscape, the net-90°-rotated (portrait-oriented) content sits in `CameraPreview`'s landscape `AspectRatio` box (`_isLandscape()` is true because `deviceOrientation` is landscape) → visible horizontal stretch. Box axis and content axis come from different frames.

## Analysis — the math is right, the frames are mixed

`ImageReaderRotatedPreview._computeRotationDegrees` (0.7.3):

```dart
double rotationDegrees =
    (sensorOrientationDegrees - currentDefaultDisplayRotationDegrees * sign + 360) % 360;
final double extraRotationDegrees =
    getPreAppliedQuarterTurnsRotationFromDeviceOrientation(orientation) * 90;
rotationDegrees -= extraRotationDegrees;
```

Fitting the measured values, the applied rotation matches this formula **exactly, with zero error in every sample**, given the display rotation values of a naturally-landscape display (window-portrait ⇔ `Surface.ROTATION_90`). The computation is internally consistent. The defect is that two inputs live in different reference frames:

- `currentDefaultDisplayRotationDegrees` — relative to the **display's natural orientation** (landscape on the unfolded panel);
- `getPreAppliedQuarterTurnsRotationFromDeviceOrientation(orientation)` and `sensorOrientationDegrees` — effectively relative to the **portrait chassis frame** (the frame in which the values are correct on the folded display).

On natural-portrait displays the two frames coincide and the formula works. On the unfolded panel they differ by one quarter turn, and the sum

```
ccw(displayRotation) + cw(preApplied(deviceOrientation))  (mod 4)
```

is **0 in every folded/phone sample and constantly 3 in every unfolded sample** across all grips — a clean signature of a frame mismatch rather than a race.

An additional consequence: the front-camera mirroring axis is chosen from `deviceOrientation` (`Transform.scale(scaleY/scaleX: -1)`, lines 151–158). A mirror about the wrong axis equals the correct mirror composed with a 180° rotation, which is exactly what users report ("rotated 180°, not flipped"), and why the error reads as 180° rather than 90°.

## Camera enumeration is fold-invariant (so apps cannot work around it by selection)

`availableCameras()` returns, byte-identical whether folded or unfolded:

```
0: back  sensorOrientation 90
1: front sensorOrientation 270
2: back  sensorOrientation 90
3: front sensorOrientation 270
```

Opening id 1 shows the user's face both folded and unfolded — physically different sensors (cover vs inner camera) behind one logical id, while the advertised `sensorOrientation` never changes. There is no signal an app could use to select differently.

## What we ruled out

- **Plugin upgrade** 0.6.24+1 → 0.7.3 (includes CameraX 1.6.0 and the 0.6.29 lens-direction change): byte-identical rotation chains before/after.
- **Stale enumeration caching in the app**: removed; enumeration verified fresh per session; fold-invariant regardless.
- **App-side geometry**: reproduced with `CameraPreview` used bare (no external constraints), so -style tight-constraint stretching is an additional symptom, not the cause.

## Expected

`ImageReaderRotatedPreview` should compute the correction in a single frame — either by converting `Display.getRotation()` into the same frame as `DeviceOrientation`/`sensorOrientation` using the display's natural orientation, or by deriving the correction purely from the `deviceOrientation` stream as the SurfaceTexture path effectively does. The mirroring axis should be chosen in the same frame.

## Actual

Preview rotated 180° (front) / axis-mismatched stretch (back) on foldable inner displays; correct on the cover display and on regular phones.

## Repro

1. Any Flutter app with `CameraPreview`, portrait-locked via `setPreferredOrientations`, targetSdk 36.
2. Run on a foldable whose inner display is naturally landscape (measured here: Z Fold 8; sw unfolded 704dp → orientation restriction ignored by Android 16).
3. Unfold, open the front camera. Preview is rotated 180° in every grip; folding restores correctness.

issues.title: [google_sign_in_android] IllegalStateException: Reply already submitted — Delegate.getCredential's CredentialManagerCallback has no guard against duplicate onError delivery
issues.body:
### Steps to Reproduce We don't have a deterministic local repro yet — this surfaced in production via Crashlytics. Based on the stack trace and the plugin source, the trigger appears to be: 1. Call `GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()` on Android (goes through `CredentialManager.getCredentialAsync()` in `GoogleSignInPlugin.java`, either via `GetSignInWithGoogleOption` (`useButtonFlow: true`) or `GetGoogleIdOption`). 2. The underlying `androidx.credentials.playservices` compat shim (`CredentialProviderController`) reports a failure to our plugin's `CredentialManagerCallback.onError` **more than once** for the same request (e.g. a duplicate/late `ResultReceiver` delivery — same general failure class as #188062, but on the sign-in path rather than the authorization path). 3. The anonymous `CredentialManagerCallback` registered in `Delegate.getCredential(...)` has no guard against being invoked twice — each invocation unconditionally calls `ResultUtilsKt.completeWithValue(callback, ...)`, which completes the underlying Pigeon `Reply`. The second completion throws. ### Expected results A duplicate/late `onError` delivery for the same `getCredentialAsync` request should be a no-op, the same way #188062's fix made duplicate `onActivityResult` deliveries a no-op for the authorization flow. ### Actual results The app crashes with an uncaught `IllegalStateException` on a background executor thread: ``` Exception java.lang.IllegalStateException: Reply already submitted at io.flutter.embedding.engine.dart.DartMessenger$Reply.reply (DartMessenger.java:425) at io.flutter.plugin.common.BasicMessageChannel$IncomingMessageHandler$1.reply (BasicMessageChannel.java:266) at io.flutter.plugins.googlesignin.GoogleSignInApi$Companion.setUp$lambda$1$0$0 (GoogleSignInApi.java:727) at io.flutter.plugins.googlesignin.ResultUtilsKt.completeWithValue (ResultUtils.kt:16) at io.flutter.plugins.googlesignin.GoogleSignInPlugin$Delegate$1.onError (GoogleSignInPlugin.java:322) at io.flutter.plugins.googlesignin.GoogleSignInPlugin$Delegate$1.onError (GoogleSignInPlugin.java:272) at androidx.credentials.playservices.controllers.CredentialProviderController.maybeReportErrorFromResultReceiver$lambda$0$0 (CredentialProviderController.java:154) at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker (ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1100) at java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run (ThreadPoolExecutor.java:624) at java.lang.Thread.run (Thread.java:1572) ``` Observed once in production on a Motorola moto g14 (Android 14, SDK 34). ### Root cause Same failure class as #188062, different code path. In `GoogleSignInPlugin.java`, `Delegate.getCredential(...)` (used by both the button-flow and lightweight-auth `getCredentialAsync` calls) registers this anonymous callback with no dedup guard: ```java CredentialManager credentialManager = credentialManagerFactory.create(context); credentialManager.getCredentialAsync( activity, requestBuilder.build(), null, Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor(), new CredentialManagerCallback<>() { @Override public void onResult(GetCredentialResponse response) { // ... always calls ResultUtilsKt.completeWithValue(callback, ...) } @Override public void onError(@NonNull GetCredentialException e) { // ... always calls ResultUtilsKt.completeWithValue(callback, ...) // no check for whether this callback has already completed } }); ``` Unlike the `authorize()` path fixed in #11984 (which had a one-shot `pendingAuthorizationCallback` field that just wasn't being cleared on the success path), this `getCredential(...)` callback has **no one-shot guard at all** — any second invocation of either `onResult` or `onError` from the Play Services compat layer will unconditionally attempt to complete the same Pigeon `Reply` again. ### Notes - Likely same underlying Play Services `ResultReceiver` re-delivery behavior as #188062 (e.g. activity recreation / process state changes), but manifesting through `CredentialProviderController.maybeReportErrorFromResultReceiver` on the sign-in (`getCredential`) path instead of the authorization (`onActivityResult`) path. - Fix in #11984 doesn't cover this path since it only touched `Delegate.onActivityResult`'s `pendingAuthorizationCallback` field, which is unrelated to the `getCredential(...)` anonymous callback. - Low volume in our production Crashlytics (2 occurrences in ~18h across ~thousands of daily active users), consistent with a rare re-delivery race rather than something hit on every sign-in. ### Versions - `google_sign_in: 7.2.0` - `google_sign_in_android: 7.2.16` - Flutter 3.44.9 (stable), Dart 3.12.2 - Affected device (observed): Motorola moto g14, Android 14 (SDK 34)
flutter doctor -v ``` [✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.44.9, on macOS, locale en-US) • Flutter version 3.44.9 on channel stable • Framework revision 6b182d2c75 (6 days ago) • 2026-08-05 • Engine revision b9499e4c25212536ba3a4eec4f5c1905fb3214fe • Dart version 3.12.2 • DevTools 2.57.0 ```

issues.title: Actions.handler always returns null since 3.47.0 (Actions.maybeFind no longer forwards intent type)
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Register an `Action` for a custom `Intent` subtype via an `Actions` widget:
   ```dart
   Actions(
     actions: <Type, Action<Intent>>{
       MyIntent: CallbackAction<MyIntent>(onInvoke: (intent) { ... }),
     },
     child: ...,
   )
   ```
2. Further down the tree, resolve a callback with:
   ```dart
   final callback = Actions.handler(context, MyIntent(...));
   ```
3. `callback` is always `null`, even though a matching `Actions` ancestor exists.

### Expected results

`Actions.handler<T>()` finds the registered `Action<T>` for the intent's runtime type and returns a working `VoidCallback`, as it did before 3.47.0.

### Actual results

`Actions.handler` always returns `null`.

### Root cause

`Actions.handler` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/actions.dart`) was changed by #180883 ("Fix some type checks in the `Actions` widget") from:

```dart
static VoidCallback? handler<T extends Intent>(BuildContext context, T intent) {
  final Action<T>? action = Actions.maybeFind<T>(context);
  ...
}
```

to:

```dart
static VoidCallback? handler<T extends Intent>(BuildContext context, T intent) {
  final Action<Intent>? action = Actions.maybeFind(context);
  ...
}
```

The new call no longer passes an explicit type argument `<T>` nor the `intent:` parameter. Dart's downward type inference resolves `maybeFind`'s type parameter from the declared local variable type (`Action<Intent>?`), so it infers `T = Intent` instead of the caller's actual intent type. Inside `maybeFind` -> `_getActionForIntent<T>`, the lookup key becomes:

```dart
actionsMarker.actions[intent?.runtimeType ?? T]
```

Since `intent` was never forwarded, this evaluates to `actionsMarker.actions[Intent]` (the literal `Intent` type) instead of the registered subtype key (e.g. `MyIntent`). Apps register actions keyed by their concrete `Intent` subtype, not by `Intent` itself, so the lookup always misses and `Actions.handler` returns `null` universally, for any intent type.

`Actions.invoke` / `Actions.maybeInvoke` are unaffected, since they forward `intent` directly to `_getActionForIntent`.

### Suggested fix

Forward the intent and type explicitly in `Actions.handler`:

```dart
static VoidCallback? handler<T extends Intent>(BuildContext context, T intent) {
  final Action<Intent>? action = Actions.maybeFind<T>(context, intent: intent);
  ...
}
```

### Flutter/Dart/Device info

```
Flutter 3.47.0 • channel stable • revision 4cf24164269a5ebf0c16a028a00727d0e77bbb05
Engine • revision 5f77625673248ee5846fbcaf5d3e1a3878386fd7
Dart 3.13.0
```

Regressed by commit f7689c75128b3c8d496b42761d68bcbe84dd9891 (#180883), first shipped in `3.47.0-0.1.pre`, present in `3.47.0` stable.

issues.title: Destination Hero child State is recreated multiple times during a Hero transition
`AnalysisOptionsMigration` ignores `include:`, repeatedly rewriting `analysis_options.yaml` files that already inherit the exclusions
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

`AnalysisOptionsMigration` (added in #187940, shipped in 3.47.0) decides whether a project needs migrating by reading only the literal contents of that project's own `analysis_options.yaml`. It never resolves `include:`, so a project that already inherits the exclusions from a shared analysis options file gets rewritten anyway, on every command that calls `ensureReadyForPlatformSpecificTooling` (`flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter run`, `flutter build`).

From a stock `flutter create repro`:

1. Move the analyzer config into `repro/shared_options.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml

   analyzer:
     exclude:
       - build/**
       - android/**
       - ios/**
       - web/**
       - windows/**
       - macos/**
       - linux/**
   ```
2. Reduce `repro/analysis_options.yaml` to `include: shared_options.yaml`
3. Confirm the inherited exclusions really are in effect. `dart analyze` doesn't run the migration, so it sees the unmodified file:
   ```console
   $ printf 'int probe() => "nope";\n' > android/probe.dart && dart analyze
   No issues found!

   $ printf 'int probe() => "nope";\n' > lib/probe.dart && dart analyze
     error - lib/probe.dart:1:16 - A value of type 'String' can't be returned ... - return_of_invalid_type
   ```
   `android/` is excluded, `lib/` is still analyzed. The shared config works.
4. `flutter analyze`

### Expected results

No migration. The project already excludes every directory in `excludesToExclude`.

### Actual results

```console
$ flutter analyze
Upgrading analysis_options.yaml to exclude build and platform directories.
```

The file is rewritten to re-add the seven exclusions locally, duplicating what the included file already provides. Reverting and re-running any Flutter command adds them straight back, so there's no way to keep the config centralized.

This hurts monorepos with a shared lints package. [supabase/supabase-flutter](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-flutter) publishes a `supabase_lints` package that all 20 workspace packages include; putting the exclusions there analyzes correctly, but `flutter pub get` still rewrites all 20 files, so a routine `pub get` leaves every contributor with a 20-file dirty working tree.

### Suggested fix

Title: `AnalysisOptionsMigration` ignores `include:`, repeatedly rewriting `analysis_options.yaml` files that already inherit the exclusions

Description:
### Steps to reproduce

`AnalysisOptionsMigration` (added in , shipped in 3.47.0) decides whether a project needs migrating by reading only the literal contents of that project's own `analysis_options.yaml`. It never resolves `include:`, so a project that already inherits the exclusions from a shared analysis options file gets rewritten anyway, on every command that calls `ensureReadyForPlatformSpecificTooling` (`flutter pub get`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter run`, `flutter build`).

From a stock `flutter create repro`:

1. Move the analyzer config into `repro/shared_options.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   include: package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml

   analyzer:
     exclude:
       - build/**
       - android/**
       - ios/**
       - web/**
       - windows/**
       - macos/**
       - linux/**
   ```
2. Reduce `repro/analysis_options.yaml` to `include: shared_options.yaml`
3. Confirm the inherited exclusions really are in effect. `dart analyze` doesn't run the migration, so it sees the unmodified file:
   ```console
   $ printf 'int probe() => "nope";\n' > android/probe.dart && dart analyze
   No issues found!

   $ printf 'int probe() => "nope";\n' > lib/probe.dart && dart analyze
     error - lib/probe.dart:1:16 - A value of type 'String' can't be returned ... - return_of_invalid_type
   ```
   `android/` is excluded, `lib/` is still analyzed. The shared config works.
4. `flutter analyze`

### Expected results

No migration. The project already excludes every directory in `excludesToExclude`.

### Actual results

```console
$ flutter analyze
Upgrading analysis_options.yaml to exclude build and platform directories.
```

The file is rewritten to re-add the seven exclusions locally, duplicating what the included file already provides. Reverting and re-running any Flutter command adds them straight back, so there's no way to keep the config centralized.

This hurts monorepos with a shared lints package. supabase/supabase-flutter publishes a `supabase_lints` package that all 20 workspace packages include; putting the exclusions there analyzes correctly, but `flutter pub get` still rewrites all 20 files, so a routine `pub get` leaves every contributor with a 20-file dirty working tree.

### Suggested fix

`analysis_options_migration.dart#L50-L65` inspects `root['analyzer']['exclude']` directly after `loadYamlNode`. Resolving `include:` (relative paths and `package:` URIs) before computing `needsMigration` would make it a no-op whenever the effective options already carry the exclusions, whichever file in the chain declares them.

If full include resolution is too costly for a path that runs on every command, a narrower fix would be to skip the migration when the local file is only an `include:` directive, or to add an opt-out flag.

issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

In an internationalized app with .arb files. 
1) Migrate to flutter 3.47 and standalone UI packages following those instructions: https://flutter.dev/blog/whats-new-in-flutter-3-47
2) Execute: 
```console 
flutter gen-l10n
```


### Expected results

The localization file (app_localizations.dart with below configuration) compatible with standalone UI package according to migration guide: https://flutter.dev/blog/whats-new-in-flutter-3-47:
```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:material_ui/material_ui.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart' as intl;

...

  ///
  /// Additional delegates can be added by appending to this list in
  /// MaterialApp. This list does not have to be used at all if a custom list
  /// of delegates is preferred or required.
  static const List<LocalizationsDelegate<dynamic>> localizationsDelegates = <LocalizationsDelegate<dynamic>>[
    delegate,
    ...GlobalMaterialLocalizations.delegates,
  ];

...
```

### Actual results

Below is the generated localization file (app_localizations.dart with below configuration), depending on embedded UI packages. 

```dart
import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:flutter_localizations/flutter_localizations.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart' as intl;

...

  /// A list of this localizations delegate along with the default localizations
  /// delegates.
  ///
  /// Returns a list of localizations delegates containing this delegate along with

  /// and GlobalWidgetsLocalizations.delegate.

  /// Additional delegates can be added by appending to this list in

    delegate,

...
```

issues.title: Plugin with compileSdkExtension triggers bogus "compiles against Android SDK 2147483647" warning
issues.body:
## Steps to reproduce

Any Android plugin that sets `compileSdkExtension` triggers a spurious `compileSdk` warning in consuming apps, because Flutter's Gradle tooling cannot parse the resulting platform hash string.

1. In an Android plugin's `android/build.gradle`, set both a `compileSdk` and a `compileSdkExtension`:

   ```gradle
   android {
       compileSdk = 36
       compileSdkExtension = 19
   }
   ```

   (This is not exotic — it is mandatory for anything depending on `androidx.health.connect:connect-client:1.2.0-alpha03`, whose AAR metadata declares `minCompileSdk=36` / `minCompileSdkExtension=19`.)

2. Consume that plugin from an app with a *higher* plain `compileSdk`, e.g. `compileSdk = 37`.

3. `flutter build apk --release`

## Expected results

No warning. The plugin compiles against API 36 (extension 19); the app compiles against API 37. The app's `compileSdk` is not lower than the plugin's, so there is nothing to warn about.

## Actual results

```
Your project is configured to compile against Android SDK 37, but the following plugin(s) require to be compiled against a higher Android SDK version:
- health_connector_hc_android compiles against Android SDK 2147483647
Fix this issue by compiling against the highest Android SDK version (they are backward compatible).
Add the following to .../android/app/build.gradle.kts:

    android {
        compileSdk = 2147483647
        ...
    }
```

`2147483647` is `Int.MAX_VALUE`, and the suggested fix is impossible to apply.

## Root cause

`FlutterPluginUtils.getCompileSdkFromProject` extracts the compile SDK by blindly stripping the first 8 characters (`android-`) off AGP's platform hash string:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterPluginUtils.kt#L509-L510

```kotlin
internal fun getCompileSdkFromProject(project: Project): String =
    getLegacyAndroidExtension(project).compileSdkVersion!!.substring(8)
```

When `compileSdkExtension` is set, AGP's `AndroidVersion.getPlatformHashString()` appends the extension level, so `compileSdkVersion` is `"android-36-ext19"` rather than `"android-36"`. `substring(8)` therefore yields `"36-ext19"`.

That value then flows into two places, both of which mishandle it:

**1. `detectLowCompileSdkVersionOrNdkVersion`** — falls back to `Int.MAX_VALUE`:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterPluginUtils.kt#L726-L727

```kotlin
val pluginCompileSdkVersion: Int =
    getCompileSdkFromProject(pluginProject).toIntOrNull() ?: Int.MAX_VALUE
```

`"36-ext19".toIntOrNull()` is `null`, so the plugin is treated as requiring API 2147483647. The comment on L698-699 shows the fallback was intended for *preview* SDKs (`android-Baklava`); the `-extNN` suffix was not considered.

**2. `PluginHandler`** — string-compares the raw value:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/plugins/PluginHandler.kt#L124-L132

```kotlin
val projectCompileSdkVersion: String = getCompileSdkFromProject(project)
val pluginCompileSdkVersion: String = getCompileSdkFromProject(pluginProject)
if (pluginCompileSdkVersion > projectCompileSdkVersion) { ... }
```

This produces its own wrong answers for extension strings — e.g. `"36-ext19" > "36"` is `true`, so a plugin on API 36 ext 19 warns against an app on plain API 36. (The existing TODO on L126-128 already flags this comparison as unsound for preview versions.)

## Impact

The warning is cosmetic — `logPluginCompileSdkWarnings` is logger-only and the build succeeds — but it is unactionable and misleading. Plugin authors who depend on any AAR requiring an SDK extension have no way to silence it: removing `compileSdkExtension` makes AGP's AAR metadata check fail, and keeping it produces this warning on every consumer build. It has already led to churn in at least one plugin repo trying to "fix" a bug that isn't theirs.

## Suggested fix

Parse the extension suffix instead of discarding it. For the API-level comparison, the base API level is the meaningful number:

```kotlin
internal fun getCompileSdkFromProject(project: Project): String =
    getLegacyAndroidExtension(project).compileSdkVersion!!
        .substring(8)
        .substringBefore("-ext")
```

That makes `"android-36-ext19"` yield `"36"`, which parses cleanly and compares correctly in both call sites. If the extension level should participate in the comparison, it would need to be surfaced as a separate field rather than folded into the string.

## Flutter Doctor output

<details><summary>flutter doctor -v</summary>

```
[√] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.44.8, on Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26200.8973], locale en-IN)
    • Flutter version 3.44.8 on channel stable at C:\Users\Devasy\Downloads\flutter
    • Upstream repository https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git
    • Framework revision 058e0af2c2 (3 weeks ago), 2026-07-23 10:56:21 -0700
```

issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Minimal project attached (a bare `PlatformViewLink` + `AndroidViewSurface` over a plain Android `View` that only logs and draws the `MotionEvent`s it receives — no WebView, no plugins).

On a physical Android device:

1. Press and hold on the left half, moving in circles.
2. With that finger still down, press and hold on the right half.
3. Release the **left** finger only.
4. Press the left half again.

### Expected results

Each pointer keeps reporting its own finger's position. Pointer ids and coordinates stay paired.


### Actual results

From step 4 on, the `MotionEvent`s delivered to the platform view are corrupted:

- one pointer reports coordinates **pixel-identical** to the other finger (two real fingers cannot occupy the same pixel);
- the other pointer reports `2 * P_other - P_real` — a point reflection through the other pointer — which frequently lands outside the view bounds;
- the framework also emits a pointer-up for a finger that is still touching the screen.

Single touch is unaffected.

### Code sample

Two files. Nothing else is needed — no plugins, no dependencies beyond a default
`flutter create` project.

The platform view is a plain Android `View` that only logs the `MotionEvent`s it
receives and flags two anomalies computed from the raw event data:

- two pointers reporting **identical integer coordinates** — two real fingers cannot
  occupy the same pixel;
- a pointer whose coordinates fall **outside the view bounds**.

#### Steps

1. `flutter run` on a physical Android device (multi-touch required).
2. Press and hold on the left half, moving in circles.
3. With that finger still down, press and hold on the right half.
4. Release the **left** finger only.
5. Press the left half again.
6. `adb logcat -s MTRepro`

Expected: pointer ids stay paired with their own finger's coordinates.
Actual: `★` lines appear from step 5 on.

---

#### `android/app/src/main/kotlin/<...>/MainActivity.kt`

```kotlin
package com.example.multitouch_repro   // <-- match your package

import android.content.Context
import android.util.Log
import android.view.MotionEvent
import android.view.View
import io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivity
import io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterEngine
import io.flutter.plugin.common.StandardMessageCodec
import io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformView
import io.flutter.plugin.platform.PlatformViewFactory

class MainActivity : FlutterActivity() {
    override fun configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine: FlutterEngine) {
        super.configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine)
        flutterEngine.platformViewsController.registry
            .registerViewFactory("touch_logger", TouchLoggerFactory())
    }
}

class TouchLoggerFactory : PlatformViewFactory(StandardMessageCodec.INSTANCE) {
    override fun create(context: Context, viewId: Int, args: Any?) =
        object : PlatformView {
            private val view = TouchLoggerView(context)
            override fun getView(): View = view
            override fun dispose() {}
        }
}

class TouchLoggerView(context: Context) : View(context) {
    override fun onTouchEvent(event: MotionEvent): Boolean {
        val sb = StringBuilder()
        val seen = HashMap<String, Int>()
        var problem: String? = null

        for (i in 0 until event.pointerCount) {
            val id = event.getPointerId(i)
            val x = event.getX(i)
            val y = event.getY(i)
            sb.append(" [i=$i id=$id ${x.toInt()},${y.toInt()}]")

            val key = "${x.toInt()},${y.toInt()}"
            val prev = seen.put(key, id)
            if (prev != null && prev != id) {
                problem = "id=$prev and id=$id report identical coordinates ($key)"
            }
            if (x < -2 || y < -2 || x > width + 2 || y > height + 2) {
                problem = "id=$id at ${x.toInt()},${y.toInt()} is outside the view (${width}x$height)"
            }
        }

        val name = when (event.actionMasked) {
            MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN -> "DOWN"
            MotionEvent.ACTION_UP -> "UP"
            MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_DOWN -> "POINTER_DOWN(idx=${event.actionIndex})"
            MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP -> "POINTER_UP(idx=${event.actionIndex})"
            MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE -> "MOVE"
            MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL -> "CANCEL"
            else -> "OTHER"
        }
        Log.i("MTRepro", "$name count=${event.pointerCount}$sb")
        problem?.let { Log.e("MTRepro", "  ★ $it") }
        return true
    }
}
```

#### `lib/main.dart`

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: TouchLogger())));

class TouchLogger extends StatelessWidget {
  const TouchLogger({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return PlatformViewLink(
      viewType: 'touch_logger',
      surfaceFactory: (context, controller) => AndroidViewSurface(
        controller: controller as AndroidViewController,
        hitTestBehavior: PlatformViewHitTestBehavior.opaque,
        gestureRecognizers: const {},
      ),
      onCreatePlatformView: (params) =>
          PlatformViewsService.initExpensiveAndroidView(
            id: params.id,
            viewType: 'touch_logger',
            layoutDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
          )
            ..addOnPlatformViewCreatedListener(params.onPlatformViewCreated)
            ..create(),
    );
  }
}
```

`initExpensiveAndroidView` (Hybrid Composition) is shown because that is what
`flutter_inappwebview` uses by default. `initSurfaceAndroidView` (TLHC/VD) and a
plain `AndroidView` reproduce the same way; so does
`initHybridAndroidView` (HCPP) with
`io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableSurfaceControl` enabled on Android 13+.
Adding an `EagerGestureRecognizer` makes no difference.

### Evidence

Instrumented at three points — the framework's raw `PointerEvent`s, a 1:1 replica of `_AndroidMotionEventConverter` showing what the framework *should* be sending, and the `MotionEvent` actually received by the Android view.

At the moment of corruption (device density 2.625; logical → physical):

```
[SYNTH] POINTER_DOWN(idx=1) count=2 [id=1 347,403] [id=0 188,360]            <- framework side, correct
MTRepro POINTER_DOWN(idx=0 id=0) count=2 [i=0 id=0 912,1057] [i=1 id=1 1331,1169]   <- as received, corrupted
```

- `i=0 id=0` reports `912,1057`, which is `347,403 × 2.625` — the coordinates belonging to **id=1**.
- `i=1 id=1` reports `1331,1169`, which is `2 × P(id=1) - P(id=0)`:
  `2×912 − 188×2.625 = 1330.5` (observed 1331), `2×1057 − 360×2.625 = 1169` (observed 1169).

The reflection holds across 30+ samples to within 1px, e.g. `P(id=0) = 60,323` → predicted `2×912 − 157.5 = 1666.5`, observed `1666`.

A control comparison from the same session, before the id is reused, is correct:

```
[SYNTH] POINTER_DOWN(idx=1) count=2 [id=0 66,378] [id=1 347,403]
MTRepro POINTER_DOWN(idx=1 id=1) count=2 [i=0 id=0 172,992] [i=1 id=1 912,1057]
```

(`66,378 × 2.625 = 173,992` ≈ `172,992`; `347,403 × 2.625 = 911,1058` ≈ `912,1057`.)

### Analysis

The framework builds `pointerProperties` and `pointerCoords` from `pointerPositions.keys`
(`packages/flutter/lib/src/services/platform_views.dart`, `_AndroidMotionEventConverter.toAndroidMotionEvent`), which is a `LinkedHashMap` in **insertion** order.

That order matches ascending Android pointer id order until a released id is reused: `_remove()` returns the id to `usedAndroidPointerIds`, and the next `handlePointerDownEvent()` assigns the lowest free id to a newly pressed pointer. After the sequence above, insertion order is `[B, A]` — ids `[1, 0]`.

Engine side, `PlatformViewsController.toMotionEvent()` pops the original event from `motionEventTracker` and *translates* its coordinates rather than assigning them per pointer. The translation delta is taken positionally from the framework arrays, so a mismatched order produces a delta of `P_other − P_real` applied to every pointer — yielding exactly the two symptoms above.

So the two sides disagree about what the array order means: the framework emits insertion order, the engine reads it as ascending-id order.

### Validation

Three-way A/B in a single build, switchable at runtime, dispatching to the same platform view:

| Dispatch | Result |
|---|---|
| Framework (`dispatchPointerEvent`) | reproduces |
| Manual via `AndroidViewController.sendMotionEvent`, same ordering as the framework | reproduces |
| Manual, arrays sorted by Android pointer id | **does not reproduce**; dragging feels normal |

The middle row is the control: it establishes that the manual channel is equivalent to the framework's, so the third row's result is attributable to the ordering change alone.

### Proposed fix

Sort the pointer list by Android pointer id so both parallel arrays and the derived action index match what the engine assumes (patch attached, `flutter-fix.patch`):

```dart
final List<int> pointers = pointerPositions.keys.toList()
  ..sort((int a, int b) => pointerProperties[a]!.id.compareTo(pointerProperties[b]!.id));
```

This makes the caller satisfy the engine's expectation. It does not remove the engine's positional assumption; a complementary engine-side fix would pair coordinates by pointer id instead of by array position. Happy to send either as a PR.

One thing worth a maintainer's eye: `pointerIdx` is also used by the batching guard
`isSinglePointerAction(event) && pointerIdx < numPointers - 1`, so sorting changes which pointer counts as "last". No dropped moves were observed in testing, but that testing was two-finger and manual — 3+ finger behaviour has not been stress-tested, and this converter has had multi-touch trouble there before (#69431).

### Related

Previously reported as #157463 (closed while still labelled "in triage" / "waiting for response", no linked fix). That reporter traced it to `translateMotionEvent` and reported that Flutter 3.22.0 behaves correctly, i.e. this is a regression — we have not independently verified the 3.22.0 claim.

Real-world impact: an app embedding third-party HTML5/Godot games in a WebView. Every game using an on-screen joystick together with an action button is broken on Android; the same page in mobile Chrome behaves correctly.

```console
[Paste your logs here]
```

issues.title: Failed assertion: line 863 pos 12: '_drag == null': is not true.
`AnalysisOptionsMigration` excludes `web/**` unconditionally, silently dropping Dart web package sources from analysis
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

`AnalysisOptionsMigration` (added in #187940, shipped in 3.47.0) writes a fixed seven-entry exclusion list. It is a `const` with no relationship to what the project actually contains ([`analysis_options_migration.dart#L39-L47`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/migrations/analysis_options_migration.dart#L39-L47)), so `web/**` is written into every project — including ones where `web/` is a source directory rather than a platform scaffold.

`web/` is where the official `dart create -t web` template puts `main.dart`. One `flutter pub get` takes it out of analysis:

```console
$ dart create -t web webrepro && cd webrepro
$ ls -1
analysis_options.yaml
CHANGELOG.md
pubspec.lock
pubspec.yaml
README.md
web

$ printf 'int probe() => "nope";\n' >> web/main.dart
$ dart analyze
  error - web/main.dart:10:16 - A value of type 'String' can't be returned from the function 'probe' because it has a return type of 'int'. - return_of_invalid_type
1 issue found.

$ flutter pub get
Resolving dependencies...
Downloading packages...
Got dependencies!
Upgrading analysis_options.yaml to exclude build and platform directories.

$ dart analyze
Analyzing webrepro...
No issues found!
```

The package has no `android/`, `ios/`, `macos/`, `linux/` or `windows/` directory at all. The only one of the seven names it does have is `web/`, which holds its code — and that is the one the migration takes out of analysis. The output names no paths, so the loss of coverage is silent, and the error stays hidden until someone reads the rewritten `analysis_options.yaml`.

`flutter pub get` in a Dart-only package is not contrived: it is what happens in mixed Flutter/Dart monorepos and Dart workspaces, where the Flutter app and the pure-Dart packages sit side by side. The same layout is described in [this comment on #191056](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/191056#issuecomment-5279479483).

### The same unconditional list in a Flutter app

The mechanism is visible without any web package — a project created for two platforms gets exclusions for the four it does not have, and cannot keep them out:

```console
$ flutter create --platforms=android,ios repro_ao
$ ls -1 repro_ao
analysis_options.yaml
android
ios
lib
pubspec.lock
pubspec.yaml
README.md
repro_ao.iml
test

$ sed -n '/^analyzer:/,/^$/p' repro_ao/analysis_options.yaml
analyzer:
  exclude:
    - build/**
    - android/**
    - ios/**
    - web/**
    - windows/**
    - macos/**
    - linux/**

$ # reduce the exclude list to `- build/**`, then:
$ flutter analyze
Upgrading analysis_options.yaml to exclude build and platform directories.
Analyzing repro_ao...
```

issues.title: Adopt Detekt for Kotlin static analysis
issues.body:
Currently, the Flutter repository relies on a mix of formatting tools for Kotlin code, primarily `ktlint` and `ktformat`. While these tools are excellent for enforcing stylistic consistency (like whitespace and import ordering), they lack deeper semantic static analysis capabilities.

A specific use case we recently encountered during the AGP 9.1.0 migration was the introduction of redundant fully qualified class names (e.g., using `com.android.build.api.dsl.ApplicationExtension` inline when `ApplicationExtension` was already imported at the top of the file). That was caught in code review. 

Consider adopting **Detekt**, the standard static analysis tool for Kotlin. Detekt can catch code smells and semantic errors that formatters miss. For example, its `UnnecessaryFullyQualifiedName` rule would have automatically caught and prevented the redundant qualification issue we encountered.

Generally we agree that tool based formatting and static analysis are useful. They are more useful in languages where contributors may not have it be their primary language or when llm coding assistants author code.
