[tool] Flutter Gradle plugin breaks Gradle configuration cache: doLast closures capture Variant/Project/ApkVariantOutput (DependencyVersionChecker.configureMinSdkCheck, FlutterPlugin.addFlutterTasks)
issues.body:
Refiling #189726, which was auto-closed on 2026-08-11 for no response and locked on 2026-08-25, as the closing bot instructed. Triage asked that report for a minimal repro and whether it still occurred on 3.44.7, and never got an answer. **Both answers are below**: it reproduces from `flutter create` in two commands, and the responsible source is byte-identical on every stable release since, including current `master`. ### Steps to reproduce No sample repository is needed — a clean scaffold reproduces it: ```bash flutter create cc_repro cd cc_repro echo "org.gradle.configuration-cache=true" >> android/gradle.properties flutter build apk --debug ``` ### Expected results The build succeeds; the configuration cache entry is stored and reused. ### Actual results `BUILD FAILED`. Gradle cannot serialize the task graph, because two Flutter Gradle Plugin `doLast` closures capture configuration-time objects. **Capture site 1 — `DependencyVersionChecker.configureMinSdkCheck`** ([`DependencyVersionChecker.kt#L149-L179`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/DependencyVersionChecker.kt#L149-L179)). The `doLast` captures the AGP `Variant` (`it`) and the `Project`: ```kotlin androidComponents?.onVariants(androidComponents.selector().all()) { val minSdkCheckTask = project.tasks.register(taskName) { doLast { val minSdkVersion = getMinSdkVersion(it) // captures Variant try { checkMinSdkVersion(minSdkVersion, project.rootDir.path, project.logger) // captures Project } catch (e: DependencyValidationException) { project.extra.set(OUT_OF_SUPPORT_RANGE_PROPERTY, true) // captures Project throw e } } } ``` ``` Configuration cache state could not be cached: field `queue` of `java.util.WeakHashMap` … bean found in field `bundleConfig` of `com.android.build.api.variant.impl.ApplicationVariantImpl_Decorated` bean found in field `$it` of `com.flutter.gradle.DependencyVersionChecker$configureMinSdkCheck$1$minSdkCheckTask$1$1` bean found in field `action` of `org.gradle.api.internal.AbstractTask$TaskActionWrapper` bean found in field `actions` of task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck` of type `org.gradle.api.DefaultTask`: error writing value of type 'java.lang.ref.ReferenceQueue' 6 problems were found storing the configuration cache, 5 of which seem unique. - Task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck`: cannot serialize object of type 'DefaultConfigurationContainer' … not supported with the configuration cache. - Task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck`: cannot serialize object of type 'DefaultDependencyHandler' … not supported with the configuration cache. - Task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck`: cannot serialize object of type 'DefaultProject', a subtype of 'org.gradle.api.Project' … not supported with the configuration cache. - Task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck`: cannot serialize object of type 'PropertiesBuildService' … not supported with the configuration cache. - Task `:app:DebugMinSdkCheck`: error writing value of type 'java.lang.ref.ReferenceQueue' ``` Four of those five are disallowed-type captures, independent of the `ReferenceQueue` reflection failure. **Capture site 2 — `FlutterPlugin.addFlutterTasks`** ([`FlutterPlugin.kt#L390-L394`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterPlugin.kt#L390-L394)), `assembleTask.doLast { … output as ApkVariantOutput … }`. Re-running with `-PskipDependencyChecks=true` removes the MinSdkCheck task, and the identical failure then fires from `:app:assembleDebug`: ``` … bean found in field `services` of `com.android.build.gradle.internal.api.ApkVariantOutputImpl_Decorated` bean found in field `$output` of `com.flutter.gradle.FlutterPlugin$addFlutterTasks$2$1$1` bean found in field `actions` of task `:app:assembleDebug` of type `org.gradle.api.DefaultTask`: error writing value of type 'java.lang.ref.ReferenceQueue' 10 problems were found storing the configuration cache, 6 of which seem unique. ``` This site already carries `// TODO(gmackall): Migrate to AGPs variant api. https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/166550`. So `--android-skip-build-dependency-validation` is not a workaround: it only removes site 1. ### Additional context **Answering the triage question on #189726 — yes, it still occurs.** I inspected `configureMinSdkCheck` on each tag; the capturing `doLast` is unchanged on **3.44.7, 3.44.8, 3.44.9 and `master`**. (The build above was run on 3.44.6; the newer versions were verified by source inspection, not by re-running.) **Not JDK-25-specific.** #189726 was reported on Windows 11 / JDK 25 / AGP 9.3.0 / Gradle 9.5.0. This reproduction is Linux / **JDK 21.0.11** / AGP 9.0.1 / Gradle 9.1.0 — a different platform and toolchain, same two capture sites. The Gradle daemon's default `--add-opens` list has never included `java.base/java.lang.ref` on any Java version. **Suggested direction** (unchanged from #189726): have the `doLast` closures capture only serializable values computed at configuration time — the variant name and `minSdk.apiLevel` as plain values, `rootDir` as a `String` — or wire them as `Provider`-based task inputs, instead of capturing `Variant` / `Project` / `ApkVariantOutput`. Related: #166550, and the same class of bug previously fixed in #139325 ("Do not use project in do last"). **Workaround for users:** keep `org.gradle.configuration-cache=false` for Flutter Android builds. Note that a `GRADLE_USER_HOME/gradle.properties` entry overrides the project file, so the cache must not be force-enabled machine-wide. ### Flutter version
flutter doctor -v ``` [✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.44.6, on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 6.15.11-061511-generic, locale C.UTF-8) • Flutter version 3.44.6 on channel stable at /home/rob/development/sdk/flutter • Upstream repository https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git • Framework revision ee80f08bbf (8 weeks ago), 2026-07-08 15:02:06 -0700 • Engine revision 83675ed276 • Dart version 3.12.2 • DevTools version 2.57.0 [✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.0.0) • Platform android-36, build-tools 36.0.0 • Java version OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 21.0.11+10-1-24.04.2-Ubuntu) • All Android licenses accepted. [✓] Linux toolchain - develop for Linux desktop [✓] Network resources ``` Gradle 9.1.0, AGP 9.0.1 (both from the unmodified `flutter create` template).

issues.title: [vector_math] normalizeInto, min, max and mix write their out parameters inefficiently
issues.body:
### Package

`vector_math` (`packages/vector_math` in flutter/core-packages)

### Description

Several `Vector2`, `Vector3` and `Vector4` members that write into an `out`/`result` parameter do more work than necessary:

- `normalizeInto(out)` does `out..setFrom(this)..normalize()`: one pass copies the components into `out`, and a second pass reads them back out of `out`'s `Float32List`, computes the length and scales them. Every component is read and written twice.
- `min(a, b, result)`, `max(a, b, result)` and `mix(min, max, a, result)` assign each component through a separate setter call (`result..x = ...` `..y = ...`) instead of one `setValues` call.

Computing the result first and writing it with a single `setValues` call produces identical values and measures 4 to 16% faster in AOT on these members (neutral on dart2js), with `normalizeInto` gaining the most since it drops the second pass, for example `Vector4.normalizeInto` goes from 3.65 to 3.06 nanoseconds per call on an Apple M series laptop.

`copyInto` writes the target's storage field by field and can be aligned with the same single `setValues` pattern at no cost, for consistency.

### Expected behavior

Members that take an `out`/`result` parameter compute their result and write it once, through `setValues`, with unchanged numeric results.

A PR with the change, a benchmark comparison and regression tests follows.

issues.title: MatrixTransition.filterQuality doesn't outline performance implications if it is provided or null
issues.body:
The documentation for MatrixTransition.filterQuality says:

> The transform will be applied by re-rendering the child if filterQuality is null, otherwise it controls the quality of an ImageFilter.matrix applied to a bitmap rendering of the child.

But it is not clear when/how often the child is re-rendered if null, or what the performance implications of that are, or how setting it affects the layer structure. So it can be non-obvious to a reader when to set it and when not to.

This came up in [reviewing this PR which sets it to null for platform views](https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/12565#discussion_r3867589016).

issues.title: [Android] Migrate remaining internal `Intent.get*Extra` calls to `IntentUtils`
issues.body:
To prevent malicious apps from injecting unexpected `Intent` extras during startup, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/190249 introduces a custom lint rule banning direct `Intent.get*Extra` calls in favor of safe wrappers (`IntentUtils.safeGet...Extra`). This issue tracks migrating the remaining exempted files (`FlutterActivity`, `FlutterFragmentActivity`, `FlutterShellArgs`, and `FlutterEngineConnectionRegistry`) to use these safe wrappers, which will verify that `Intent` extra flags are sent from the Flutter app itself in debug/profile mode or otherwise block them (including in release mode). 

Files I am sure can be fully migrated:

- [ ] `FlutterActivity.java`
- [ ] `FlutterFragmentActivity.java`
- [ ] `FlutterEngineConnectionRegistry.java`

issues.title: Android: FontWeight.w500/w600 does not visually bold CJK text on Samsung devices because fallback Typeface reports the requested weight while using a Regular-only font
issues.body:
## Issue body

```markdown
### Summary

On some Samsung Android devices, Flutter CJK text does not become visually bold when using `FontWeight.w500` or `FontWeight.w600`.

Latin characters in the same `Text` widget change weight correctly, while Chinese characters remain visually identical or very close to `FontWeight.w400`.

The font size, line height, baseline, and layout are correct. Only the visible CJK font weight is incorrect.

I reproduced the same behavior with both Impeller and Skia, so this does not appear to be specific to either renderer. The issue occurs earlier, during Android font fallback resolution / SkParagraph shaping.

After instrumenting a locally built Flutter Engine, I found that Samsung's Android font manager returns an anonymous fallback typeface such as `94##fallback`. The typeface reports the requested weight (`500` or `600`) even though the underlying Samsung CJK font is a Regular-only font.

Because the reported typeface weight equals the requested weight, SkParagraph's existing synthetic-bold detection does not enable `SkFont::setEmbolden(true)`.

---

### Environment

- Flutter: 3.41.9 stable
- Dart: 3.11.5
- Device: Samsung Galaxy A56 / `SM-A566B`
- Android: Android 15
- Build fingerprint:

```text
samsung/a56xnaxx/a56x:15/AP3A.240905.015.A2/A566BXXS6AYGF_OLM6BYI8:user/release-keys
```

- Device pixel ratio: `2.8125`
- Physical resolution: `1080 × 2340`
- Logical resolution: `384 × 832`
- Android font scale: `1.0`
- Android `fontWeightAdjustment`: `0`
- Tested build modes:
  - Release with Impeller
  - Release with Skia
  - Debug with a locally built Flutter Engine

The problem was reproduced using the unmodified official Flutter 3.41.9 artifacts before testing the custom Engine workaround described below.

---

### Minimal reproduction

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(const FontWeightTestApp());
}

class FontWeightTestApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const FontWeightTestApp({super.key});

  static const sample =
      'Samsung 字体诊断 AaBb 0123456789';

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        appBar: AppBar(
          title: const Text('Samsung CJK FontWeight Test'),
        ),
        body: const Padding(
          padding: EdgeInsets.all(16),
          child: Column(
            crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
            children: [
              Text(
                'w400: $sample',
                style: TextStyle(
                  fontSize: 20,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.w400,
                ),
              ),
              SizedBox(height: 16),
              Text(
                'w500: $sample',
                style: TextStyle(
                  fontSize: 20,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.w500,
                ),
              ),
              SizedBox(height: 16),
              Text(
                'w600: $sample',
                style: TextStyle(
                  fontSize: 20,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
                ),
              ),
              SizedBox(height: 16),
              Text(
                'w700: $sample',
                style: TextStyle(
                  fontSize: 20,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.w700,
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

No custom `fontFamily`, `fontFamilyFallback`, or font asset is used.

---

### Actual result

- Latin characters such as `Samsung`, `AaBb`, and digits visibly respond to `FontWeight`.
- Chinese characters such as `字体诊断` do not visibly become bold at `w500` or `w600`.
- The Chinese glyphs remain visually close to `w400`.
- Font size and line layout remain correct.

This results in inconsistent visual weight within the same mixed Latin/CJK text run.

[![pnFFoLQ.png](https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/01/pnFFoLQ.png)](https://imgchr.com/i/pnFFoLQ)

---

### Expected result

When `FontWeight.w500`, `w600`, or `w700` is requested, CJK glyphs should either:

1. Use an actual matching CJK font face, if available; or
2. Use synthetic emboldening when the selected fallback font does not actually provide the requested weight.

At minimum, `w600` should appear visually heavier than `w400`.

### Skia and Impeller comparison

I collected Flutter text metrics for the exact same test page using both renderers.

For every sample, the following values were identical between Skia and Impeller:

- Requested `fontWeight`
- Layout width
- Layout height
- Alphabetic baseline
- Ideographic baseline
- Line count

Example:

```text
system-size12-w400:
  Impeller width: 266.2684020996094
  Skia width:     266.2684020996094

system-size12-w500:
  Impeller width: 267.3992614746094
  Skia width:     267.3992614746094

system-size12-w600:
  Impeller width: 267.8973083496094
  Skia width:     267.8973083496094
```

All height and baseline deltas were also zero.

The visual CJK weight issue was identical with both renderers. This suggests the problem is in font resolution or shaping before renderer-specific rasterization.

---

### Samsung system font configuration

Android logcat shows Samsung preloading:

```text
Typeface: Preloading /system/fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf
Typeface: Preloading /system/fonts/RobotoStatic-Regular.ttf
Typeface: Preloading /system/fonts/SECCJK-Regular.ttc
Typeface: Preloading /system/fonts/NotoSerifCJK-Regular.ttc
```

The Samsung device's `/system/etc/fonts.xml` contains:

```xml
<family lang="zh-Hans">
    <font
        weight="400"
        style="normal"
        index="2"
        postScriptName="SECCJKjp-Regular">
        SECCJK-Regular.ttc
    </font>

    <font
        weight="400"
        style="normal"
        index="2"
        fallbackFor="serif"
        postScriptName="NotoSerifCJKjp-Regular">
        NotoSerifCJK-Regular.ttc
    </font>
</family>
```

The same `SECCJK-Regular.ttc` is used with different TTC indexes for other languages:

```xml

    </font>
</family>

    <font weight="400" style="normal" index="0">
        SECCJK-Regular.ttc
    </font>
</family>

<family lang="ko">
    <font weight="400" style="normal" index="1">
        SECCJK-Regular.ttc
    </font>
</family>
```

For Simplified Chinese, only weight 400 is registered.

There is no matching CJK Medium, SemiBold, or Bold face registered for this family.

In contrast, Samsung registers `Roboto-Regular.ttf` as a variable font with `wght` values from 100 to 900. This explains why Latin text responds to `FontWeight` while Chinese fallback glyphs do not.

I instrumented:

```text
third_party/skia/modules/skparagraph/src/OneLineShaper.cpp
```

Specifically, immediately before and after the existing `font.setEmbolden(fakeBold)` call.

The diagnostic log records:

- Requested weight
- Resolved typeface family
- Resolved typeface-reported weight
- Existing SkParagraph `fakeBold` result
- Final `SkFont::isEmbolden()` value

The important runtime results were:

#### Requested w400

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=400
reportedWeight=400
originalFakeBold=0
isEmbolden=0
```

#### Requested w500

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=500
reportedWeight=500
originalFakeBold=0
isEmbolden=0
```

#### Requested w600

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=600
reportedWeight=600
originalFakeBold=0
isEmbolden=0
```

The Android font manager does not expose this typeface to SkParagraph as `SECCJK-Regular`. It exposes an anonymous family:

```text
94##fallback
```

More importantly, although the underlying CJK font is registered only as weight 400, the resolved Typeface reports the requested weight:

```text
requested 500 -> reported 500
requested 600 -> reported 600
```

---

### Relevant SkParagraph logic

The current synthetic-bold logic in `OneLineShaper.cpp` is effectively:

```cpp
int wantedWeight = block.fStyle.getFontStyle().weight();

bool fakeBold =
    wantedWeight >= SkFontStyle::kSemiBold_Weight &&
    wantedWeight - font.getTypeface()->fontStyle().weight() >= 200;

font.setEmbolden(fakeBold);
```

On this Samsung device:

```text
wantedWeight = 600
reported Typeface weight = 600
difference = 0
```

Therefore:

```text
fakeBold = false
```

SkParagraph assumes a real weight-600 face was selected, but the resulting CJK glyphs still come from the Regular-only Samsung CJK font and are not visually bold.

---

### Root cause hypothesis

The apparent failure chain is:

1. Flutter requests `FontWeight.w500` or `FontWeight.w600`.
2. Android font fallback selects Samsung's CJK fallback font.
3. The underlying CJK font available in `fonts.xml` is only `SECCJK-Regular.ttc`, registered at weight 400.
4. Android/Skia exposes the selected font to SkParagraph as an anonymous family such as `94##fallback`.
5. The returned Typeface reports the requested weight rather than the physical font face's actual available weight.
6. SkParagraph compares the requested weight with the reported Typeface weight.
7. Because both values are equal, SkParagraph concludes that synthetic bold is unnecessary.
8. `SkFont::setEmbolden(false)` is used.
9. The CJK Regular glyphs are rendered without any visual emboldening.

This appears to be an interaction between Android font fallback, Samsung's font configuration, and SkParagraph's missing-font-style detection.

---

### Confirmed experimental workaround

For diagnosis only, I treated Samsung's anonymous fallback typeface as missing the requested bold style:

```cpp
SkString familyName;
font.getTypeface()->getFamilyName(&familyName);

const bool isAnonymousFallback =

const bool originalFakeBold =
    wantedWeight >= SkFontStyle::kSemiBold_Weight &&
    wantedWeight - font.getTypeface()->fontStyle().weight() >= 200;

const bool fakeBold =
    originalFakeBold ||
    (isAnonymousFallback &&
     wantedWeight >= SkFontStyle::kMedium_Weight);

font.setEmbolden(fakeBold);
```

After applying this experimental workaround, the runtime log became:

#### Requested w500

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=500
reportedWeight=500
originalFakeBold=0
finalFakeBold=1
isEmbolden=1
```

#### Requested w600

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=600
reportedWeight=600
originalFakeBold=0
finalFakeBold=1
isEmbolden=1
```

#### Requested w400

```text
family=94##fallback
wantedWeight=400
reportedWeight=400
originalFakeBold=0
finalFakeBold=0
isEmbolden=0
```

The visual result was then correct on the Samsung test device:

- `w400` remained unchanged.
- `w500` became visibly heavier.
- `w600` became visibly heavier.
- The previously missing CJK bold effect was restored.

This confirms that synthetic emboldening can correct the issue.

The screenshot before instrumented:
[![pnFFoLQ.png](https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/01/pnFFoLQ.png)](https://imgchr.com/i/pnFFoLQ)

The screenshot after instrumented:
[![pnFFbon.png](https://s41.ax1x.com/2026/09/01/pnFFbon.png)](https://imgchr.com/i/pnFFbon)

The workaround above is not proposed as a production-ready fix.

The `##fallback` family naming is internal and may not be stable. It may also represent fallback fonts other than Samsung CJK, including:

- Other CJK fonts
- Other scripts
- Symbol fonts
- Emoji fallback fonts

A production fix should not blindly embolden every `##fallback` typeface.

Potential safer approaches might include:

1. Detecting whether the resolved font truly contains a physical face matching the requested weight.
2. Preserving the physical/declared font style before Android returns a weight-adjusted wrapper.
3. Applying synthetic bold only to unresolved CJK runs whose selected fallback has no real requested-weight face.
4. Passing explicit information from font matching to shaping indicating whether the returned weight was synthesized.
5. Comparing against the underlying font file's actual style rather than only `SkTypeface::fontStyle()`.
6. Introducing a stable signal that the selected fallback did not provide a real matching style.

---

### Why application-level workarounds are insufficient

Setting a global family such as:

```dart
ThemeData(fontFamily: 'Roboto')
```

does not solve the problem because Roboto does not contain Chinese glyphs. Chinese characters still fall back to Samsung's CJK Regular font.

Similarly:

```dart
fontFamily: 'sans-serif-medium'
```

only changes the Latin face. CJK still uses the same fallback.

Explicitly setting:

```dart
fontVariations: [
  FontVariation('wght', 600),
]
```

does not solve this case because `SECCJK-Regular.ttc` is not exposed as a CJK variable font with a usable `wght` axis.

Bundling a complete CJK font works, but significantly increases APK size and is not ideal for applications that render arbitrary OCR, Markdown, or translated content.

Painting text twice or adding same-color shadows can visually simulate bold, but these approaches affect performance, text selection, RichText behavior, accessibility, and rendering quality.

A fix in font resolution / shaping would provide the most consistent behavior.

---

### Questions for the Flutter / Skia team

1. Is it expected that Android fallback typefaces can report the requested weight even when the underlying system font configuration contains only a Regular face?
2. Should SkParagraph's `fakeMissingFontStyles` logic account for this type of Android fallback wrapper?
3. Is there a reliable API for determining whether the resolved Typeface represents a real requested-weight face versus a synthesized style match?
4. Would it be appropriate for SkParagraph to enable synthetic bold for CJK fallback runs when no physical requested-weight face exists?
5. Is `##fallback` an intentional and stable Android SkFontMgr convention, or only an internal generated family name?
6. Is there an existing upstream fix or related issue covering Samsung CJK fallback weights?
7. If the root cause belongs in Skia or Android's `SkFontMgr_android`, should this issue be transferred or reported separately?
8. What additional traces, screenshots, font tables, or test binaries would be useful?

I can provide:

- The Samsung `/system/etc/fonts.xml`
- Full filtered Engine logs
- Impeller/Skia metric comparison
- A minimal reproduction project
- Before/after screenshots
- The experimental Engine patch

issues.title: `flutter gen-l10n` does not validate placeholder `type`, allowing code injection into generated Dart from .arb files
issues.body: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new app: `flutter create bug` 2. Enable generation in pubspec.yaml (`flutter: generate: true`) and add an `l10n.yaml` + `lib/l10n/app_en.arb` as per the standard localization setup. 3. In `app_en.arb`, set a placeholder's `type` attribute to a crafted string that closes the generated method and injects a new member (see Code sample). 4. Run `flutter gen-l10n`. 5. Inspect the generated `app_localizations_en.dart`. 6. Run `dart analyze` on the generated output. Reproduced on Flutter web and on a physical device (Pixel 6a, Android 16). ### Expected results `flutter gen-l10n` should validate the placeholder `type` attribute the same way it already validates resource names (which are checked against `_isValidGetterAndMethodName`). An illegal `type` value should raise an `L10nException` and fail generation, rather than being written into source. Ideally the supported types would be allowlisted (String, int, double, num, DateTime, Object, plus the documented numeric/date format types). ### Actual results The placeholder `type` is read as a raw, unchecked string (gen_l10n_types.dart:235) and interpolated into the generated method signature (gen_l10n.dart:130, generateMethodParameters). A crafted `type` string closes the generated method early, injects arbitrary members, and reopens a declaration to absorb the remainder of the template. The resulting file is valid Dart: it compiles, and `dart analyze` reports "No issues found." The injected code executes whenever the corresponding localization getter is called (e.g. AppLocalizations.of(context).greeting(...)). The tool applies the exact identifier check it needs to the resource *name* but not to the sibling `type` field that ends up in the same generated source. ### Code sample `app_en.arb`: ```json { "@@locale": "en", "greeting": "Hello {user}", "@greeting": { "placeholders": { "user": { "type": "Object user) { print('>>> ARBITRARY DART EXECUTED FROM A TRANSLATION FILE <<<'); return 'pwned'; } String injectedByTranslation(Object" } } } } ``` Generated `app_localizations_en.dart` after `flutter gen-l10n`: ```dart class AppLocalizationsEn extends AppLocalizations { AppLocalizationsEn([String locale = 'en']) : super(locale); @override String greeting(Object user) { print('>>> ARBITRARY DART EXECUTED FROM A TRANSLATION FILE <<<'); // injected return 'pwned'; } String injectedByTranslation(Object user) { // injected member return 'Hello $user'; } } ``` `dart analyze` on the generated file returns "No issues found!". ### Screenshots or Video ### Logs _No response_ ### Flutter Doctor output N/A

issues.title: Removing/renaming an asset requires a full rebuild, not just hot restart
issues.body:
### Use case

Rearranging asset files (delete/rename) during dev is a tedious operation today. With `flutter run` active:

- Adding an asset → picked up on hot restart. Fine.
- Removing or renaming an asset → app keeps throwing `Unable to load asset` even after a full hot **restart** (`R`). Only a full stop + `flutter run` clears it.

This forces stopping the running session before touching the assets folder — can't verify a rename/cleanup live, have to do it "offline" then relaunch. Breaks the fast dev-loop hot restart is supposed to give.

Checked existing reports — closest are #163046 and #29184, both closed as "working as intended," and both about *additions*, not *removals/renames*. Neither addresses this specific case.

### Proposal

Hot restart already re-resolves the asset manifest from `pubspec.yaml`/disk for new files — extend the same manifest refresh to also drop entries for files that no longer exist, so a stale/removed asset reference fails cleanly (or shows the intended fallback) right after hot restart, without requiring a full stop-and-rebuild.

issues.title: Flutter Gradle plugin rejects AGP Built-in Kotlin version
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

AGP 9 supports Built-in Kotlin via `android.builtInKotlin=true`.

When migrating an existing Flutter app to Built-in Kotlin, the Flutter Gradle
plugin rejects the build during configuration:

Error: Your project's Kotlin version (2.2.10) is lower than Flutter's minimum
supported version of 2.2.20.

The version cannot be upgraded independently because Built-in Kotlin is bundled
with AGP. AGP 9.4.0 (latest stable as of 2026-09-02), as well as
9.5.0-alpha03, bundle Kotlin 2.2.10.

Environment:
```
- Flutter 3.47.2
- AGP 9.3.2
- Gradle 9.7.1
- `android.builtInKotlin=true`
```

Expected behavior:
Flutter should support AGP Built-in Kotlin, or document a compatible AGP version.
The KGP version validation should not reject a version that is bundled and
controlled by AGP.

Actual behavior:
The build fails while applying `dev.flutter.flutter-gradle-plugin`, before
project tasks are configured.

Stack trace:
`com.flutter.gradle.DependencyVersionChecker.checkKGPVersion`


```
1. Create or migrate a Flutter app to AGP 9.
2. Set android.builtInKotlin=true in android/gradle.properties.
3. Remove org.jetbrains.kotlin.android / kotlin-android from Android Gradle files.
4. Run an Android Gradle task, for example fvm flutter build apk.
5. Observe the Kotlin minimum-version validation failure.
Environment: Flutter 3.47.2, AGP 9.3.2, Gradle 9.7.1.
```

### Expected results

Flutter should support AGP Built-in Kotlin or skip KGP version validation when android.builtInKotlin=true. If a newer AGP is required, Flutter should report the required compatible AGP version.

### Actual results

Error: Your project's Kotlin version (2.2.10) is lower than Flutter's
minimum supported version of 2.2.20.
The failure occurs while applying dev.flutter.flutter-gradle-plugin, in:
com.flutter.gradle.DependencyVersionChecker.checkKGPVersion
Built-in Kotlin is provided by AGP, so its version cannot be upgraded independently. AGP 9.4.0 and 9.5.0-alpha03 still bundle Kotlin 2.2.10.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

## android/gradle.properties
android.builtInKotlin=true
android.newDsl=false

## android/settings.gradle

plugins {
    id "dev.flutter.flutter-plugin-loader" version "1.0.0"
    id "com.android.application" version "9.3.2" apply false
}
##  android/app/build.gradle

plugins {
    id "com.android.application"
    id "dev.flutter.flutter-gradle-plugin"
}

</details>

issues.title: iOS ProMotion: a playing video_player texture makes the engine redraw the last layer tree every vsync (120 Hz) for 30 fps content
issues.body:
Refiling #188616, which was closed and locked before I could come back with what
was asked for there: a minimal repro, timeline traces and `flutter doctor -v` on
a current stable. Filed per #74833.

Repro: https://github.com/Ahlisen/flutter-promotion-video-repro

## What happens

A full-screen 30 fps video through `video_player`'s texture path, sitting at
rest, nothing else on screen animating. The raster thread produces 119.9
frames/s and spends 118.8 ms/s in `Rasterizer::DrawToSurfaces`. Swapping the
video for a static `Image` of its own first frame drops that to 0.3 frames/s and
0.3 ms/s.

## Expected

At rest on 30 fps content the scene recomposites near the content rate, the way
a native `AVPlayerLayer` does, rather than once per 120 Hz vsync.

## Measurements

Profile mode, ~8 s of VM timeline per arm:

| Arm | frames rasterized | of which redraw the last layer tree | raster ms/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 fps video, `video_player` texture path | 119.9 /s | 119.2 /s | 118.8 |
| the video's first frame as a static `Image` | 0.3 /s | 0 | 0.3 |
| nothing on screen | 0.1 /s | 0 | 0.1 |

The 0.1-0.3 frames/s in the last two arms is the repro's own stats overlay
ticking every five seconds, so the pipeline is alive in all three arms. Only the
live texture pins it to 120.

The three arms are switched over the VM service by the driver in the repro's
`tool/`, so this is one build with no tapping in between.

## Where the 120 frames come from

In the video arm, 666 of the 670 frames rasterized are
`Animator::DrawLastLayerTrees` and only 2 are `Rasterizer::DoDraw`. The engine
requests a vsync and re-rasterizes the previous layer tree once per vsync for as
long as a live external texture exists. The video decodes at 30 fps, so three of
every four of those frames redraw a texture that has not changed.

In the two arms without a texture, every frame that does happen is a
`Rasterizer::DoDraw` and there are no `DrawLastLayerTrees` at all.

A side effect worth knowing on its own: because no new layer tree is produced,
`SchedulerBinding` frame timings never see these frames. The app's own
`FrameTiming` counter reads 0.2 fps while the raster thread is doing 119.9. An
app measuring its own frame cost through `addTimingsCallback` will not see the
cost of a video texture at all, which is presumably why this is easy to miss.

## The `preferredFrameRateRange` suggestion from #188616

I was asked to try configuring `preferredFrameRateRange` from native code by
reference to #107902. I did: `ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift` in the repro has a
`capDisplayLinkHz` constant that adds an app-level `CADisplayLink` with
`preferredFrameRateRange` pinned to 30 Hz, exactly as that issue describes. It
makes no difference:

| | frames rasterized | of which redraw the last tree |
|---|---|---|
| stock | 119.9 /s | 119.2 /s |
| `capDisplayLinkHz = 30` | 119.9 /s | 119.8 /s |

That trace is `trace_video_cap30hz.json` in the archive linked below. The app's display
link is only a second frame-rate request for CoreAnimation to arbitrate; the
engine's own vsync client still asks for the full rate, and the higher request
wins. Nothing reachable from app code changes what the engine asks for, which is
why I do not think there is an app-side workaround for this.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/Ahlisen/flutter-promotion-video-repro and set `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` in `ios/Runner.xcodeproj` to your
   own team.
2. `flutter run --profile --trace-skia -d <promotion-iphone>`.
3. Leave it on the `VIDEO` arm, record a timeline, count
   `Rasterizer::DrawToSurfaces`: ~120/s.
4. Tap `IMAGE`, repeat: ~0.3/s.

`tool/ablate.dart` and `tool/summarise.dart` do steps 3 and 4 over the VM
service and print the table above.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.47.2 stable, framework d3b14c8769, engine a804b26164, Dart 3.13.2
- iPhone 15 Pro (A17 Pro), iOS 18.7.8, ProMotion
- Impeller (default), `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true`
- `video_player` 2.14.0 / `video_player_avfoundation` 2.11.1 from pub, default
  `VideoViewType.textureView`
- Xcode 26.3, macOS 15.7.1

## The questions asked on #188616

- Timeline traces: [`traces.zip`](https://github.com/Ahlisen/flutter-promotion-video-repro/releases/download/measurements/traces.zip)
  — one JSON per arm, plus the 30 Hz display-link run.
- Latest stable: this is 3.47.2, the current stable.
- Video: [recording-flutter-3.47.0.mp4](https://github.com/Ahlisen/flutter-promotion-video-repro/releases/download/measurements/recording-flutter-3.47.0.mp4),
  filmed on a second phone. It is not worth much here: the bug is invisible, the
  video looks the same whether the engine redraws it 30 or 120 times a second,
  so the recording only shows a video playing. It is also of the 3.47.0 build,
  taken shortly before I upgraded to 3.47.2 to re-measure. The traces are the
  evidence.
- iOS 26 comparison: I do not have a ProMotion device on iOS 26, so I cannot
  provide one.
- `flutter analyze` on the repro is clean.

## Related

- #159392 — same effect on Android variable-refresh-rate devices
- #107902 — iOS adaptive refresh rate
- #86613 — `video_player`: PlatformView on iOS/macOS

issues.title: [FKA] Keyboard focus resets to the top of the list after navigating back
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the a11y assessments app from flutter repo and build the app in iPad/iPhone
2. Enable Full Keyboard Access on the iPad.
3. Connect a physical keyboard.
4. Launch the application.
5. Navigate through the list of interactive elements using the Tab key.
6. Move focus to an element in the list, for example AutoComplete.
7. Press Space to activate/select the focused element.
8. Navigate back to the previous screen.
9. Observe where the keyboard focus is placed.

### Expected results

When returning to the previous screen, keyboard focus should be restored to the element that had focus before navigation.

For example, if AutoComplete had focus before navigating away, focus should return to AutoComplete when the user comes back.

### Actual results

When navigating back, the keyboard focus is reset to the first/top element in the list (AboutListTile) instead of returning to the previously focused element.

**Note**

- VoiceOver:  Focus remains at the same position when returning. 
- Full Keyboard Access / Physical Keyboard:  Focus moves to the top of the screen.


### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
[Paste your code here]
```

</details>


### Screenshots or Video

issues.title: [iOS][SPM] Silent native launch crash (dyld symbol not found) with zero Flutter/Dart diagnostics on transitive Swift Package version drift
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an iOS plugin that pulls in a Swift Package (via Flutter's SPM plugin support) whose own Package.swift declares an *open* version range for a transitive dependency (e.g. `.package(url: ..., from: "14.1.0")`), while a sibling package ships a *prebuilt binary* XCFramework compiled against that exact 14.1.0 API.
2. Let SPM resolve the open-range dependency to a newer minor version whose public API removed/renamed a symbol the prebuilt binary links against (e.g. 14.4.0 instead of 14.1.0).
3. Run `flutter run` (or `flutter build ios` + install) against a real device or simulator.
4. Observe: the build succeeds ("Xcode build done" is printed), then the app crashes instantly at launch with no further Flutter/Dart output.
5. `flutter clean`, deleting `build/`, `DerivedData`, and `Podfile.lock` does NOT fix it, because `ios/Runner.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved` is committed to git and SPM just re-resolves to the same broken pin.

Concrete case we hit: the `zendesk_messaging` plugin's native SDK (`ZendeskSDKMessaging` 2.36.0) ships as a prebuilt binary compiled against `ZendeskSDKUIComponents` 14.1.0, but `sdk_messaging_ios`'s own `Package.swift` declares `.package(name: "ZendeskSDKUIComponents", url: "https://github.com/zendesk/sdk_ui_components_ios", from: "14.1.0")`. SPM resolves that open range to the newest 14.x (14.4.0), which removed the `MessageFooterRendering` symbol the prebuilt binary depends on.


### Expected results

When the built app crashes at native launch (dyld/DYLD_* termination), `flutter run`/`flutter build ios` should surface at least a pointer to the failure — e.g. detect the process died immediately post-launch and print the relevant crash reason (symbol/framework name) from the .ips report, or point the developer at ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/. Ideally, `flutter build ios` would also flag when a plugin's committed Package.resolved contains a version outside the range its own transitive Package.swift declares, since that's a strong signal of an ABI-incompatible resolution.


### Actual results

`flutter run` prints "Xcode build done" and the app then hangs or exits immediately — no splash, no Dart error, nothing in the Flutter/Dart console pointing to a native crash. The only way to diagnose it is manually parsing the macOS crash report:

F=$(ls -t ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Runner-*.ips | head -1)
tail -n +2 "$F" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; t=json.load(sys.stdin).get("termination",{}); print(t.get("namespace"),t.get("indicator")); [print(r) for r in (t.get("reasons") or [])]'

which reveals:

DYLD Symbol missing
Symbol not found: _$s22ZendeskSDKUIComponents22MessageFooterRenderingVMn
  Referenced from: .../ZendeskSDKMessaging.framework/ZendeskSDKMessaging
  Expected in:     .../ZendeskSDKUIComponents.framework/ZendeskSDKUIComponents

Full write-up of the root cause and our workaround (manually pinning 9 transitive Package.resolved entries to an ABI-compatible set) is here: https://gist.github.com/VB10/c426365322267e2892ed8a6342c5d4ab


### Code sample

Minimal repro isn't practical to attach directly since it depends on a specific third-party SDK version drift; a full worked example (Package.resolved diff, the exact broken vs. working pins, and the verification commands) is in this gist: https://gist.github.com/VB10/c426365322267e2892ed8a6342c5d4ab


### Screenshots or Video

N/A — this is a launch crash with no visual symptom (nothing renders before the crash).


### Logs

`flutter run --verbose` output ends right after "Xcode build done" with no further lines. Full native crash report (.ips) and verbose log attached in gist:  https://gist.github.com/VB10/c426365322267e2892ed8a6342c5d4ab

issues.title: [Android] AccessibilityBridge's API-34 high-contrast lambda fails class verification on pre-34 devices (NoClassDefFoundError at launch)
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

> **Steps 1-4 are deterministic on any machine and prove the defect is in every release build.**
> Step 5 is the device-dependent manifestation — the reason this reaches you as a crash report
> rather than a local repro.

```
1. Any Flutter app on 3.47.0 or later (reproduced on 3.47.0 and 3.47.2), built for Android
   with minSdk 24, compileSdk 36, AGP 9.1.0, R8 enabled (i.e. a stock `--release` build).

2. flutter build appbundle --release

3. Find the obfuscated name of AccessibilityBridge and its synthetic lambdas in
   build/app/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt:

     io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge -> io.flutter.view.a
     io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge$$ExternalSyntheticLambda1 -> t2

4. Extract the DEX from the AAB and disassemble the constructor:

     dexdump -d classes4.dex   # the DEX containing io.flutter.view.a

   Observe in AccessibilityBridge.<init>:

     sget          v0, Landroid/os/Build$VERSION;.SDK_INT:I
     const/16      v1, #int 34
     if-lt         v0, v1, 0040
     003a: new-instance  v0, Lt2;        <-- API-34 lambda, never executes below 34
     0040: new-instance  v0, Ll;         <-- the no-op lambda
     0045: iput-object   v0, v2, Lio/flutter/view/a;.<field>:Lb3;   <-- the type join

   Lt2; declares Landroid/app/UiModeManager$ContrastChangeListener; (API 34) and has
   onContrastChanged(F)V. No stub for that interface exists in any DEX in the bundle.

5. Run that build on a pre-34 device whose ART eagerly resolves the type join at 0045.
   The app dies at launch. Not every pre-34 device does this - most ART builds tolerate the
   unresolved join - which is why this presents as a small, persistent slice of users rather
   than a universal failure.
```

### Expected results

The app launches. A version-gated branch that never executes on the device should not prevent
io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge from loading, and AccessibilityBridge.<init> should contain
no API-34 types in its verifiable body.

### Actual results

The app cannot launch at all on an affected device. FlutterView.attachToFlutterEngine constructs
AccessibilityBridge unconditionally, so the process dies in Activity.performStart before a single
line of Dart runs. No accessibility service needs to be enabled.

Fatal Exception: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Lt2;
    at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init>(AccessibilityBridge.java:428)
    at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init>(AccessibilityBridge.java:447)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterView.attachToFlutterEngine(FlutterView.java:1225)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivityAndFragmentDelegate.onCreateView(...:437)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterFragment.onCreateView(FlutterFragment.java:1121)
    at androidx.fragment.app.Fragment.performCreateView(Fragment.java:3115)
    ...
    at android.app.Activity.performStart(Activity.java:8330)
    at android.app.ActivityThread.handleStartActivity(ActivityThread.java:3670)

Caused by java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: t2

Device is Android 12/13 by the frames (Looper.loopOnce:201 / loop:288,
ActivityThread.main:7872, and jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe, which libcore moved to in S).

Mechanism: ART resolves the synthetic while verifying the type join of the ternary's two
branches at the iput-object, even though the if-lt means the API-34 branch never executes. The
superinterface does not exist below API 34, so DexFile.defineClass fails - and because it
swallows the NoClassDefFoundError into `suppressed` and returns null, the loader surfaces it as
ClassNotFoundException.

Seen on four consecutive releases of a production app. `Lt2;` is only R8's name for the
synthetic and varies per build; an earlier release crashed as `Lio/flutter/view/a;` - same
failure, different name.

### Code sample

> The form asks for a `flutter create bug` reproduction. There isn't a Dart-level one: the defect
> is in the engine's Java and manifests only on specific ART builds. Say so explicitly and give the
> engine source instead — that is what a triager needs here.

```
No Dart-level reproduction is possible: the defect is in the engine's Android embedding, and any
Flutter app built in release mode carries it. The offending code is:

// engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/view/AccessibilityBridge.java:426-432
private final ContrastChangedListener highContrastObserver =
    (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= API_LEVELS.API_34)
        ? (ContrastChangedListener & UiModeManager.ContrastChangeListener)
            contrast -> setHighContrastFlag()
        : contrast -> {
          /* no-op */
        };

The SDK_INT guard is correct, and registerHighContrastObserver (:718) is properly annotated
@RequiresApi(API_LEVELS.API_34). The bug is that the guarded TYPE appears inside <init>'s
verifiable body: the intersection cast

    (ContrastChangedListener & UiModeManager.ContrastChangeListener)

forces D8's desugared lambda to implement the API-34 interface, and the ternary puts it in a
type join the verifier must check on every device.

PROPOSED FIX - the precedent is already in this file. AccessibilityBridge gained an Api31Impl
holder in #184630 (8ad7de9c41e) for the same class of bug, and its javadoc states exactly the
rule this initializer breaks:

  /**
   * Isolates API-31 field references so that ART's class verifier does not attempt to resolve

Title: [Android] AccessibilityBridge's API-34 high-contrast lambda fails class verification on pre-34 devices (NoClassDefFoundError at launch)

Description:
### Steps to reproduce

> **Steps 1-4 are deterministic on any machine and prove the defect is in every release build.**
> Step 5 is the device-dependent manifestation — the reason this reaches you as a crash report
> rather than a local repro.

```
1. Any Flutter app on 3.47.0 or later (reproduced on 3.47.0 and 3.47.2), built for Android
   with minSdk 24, compileSdk 36, AGP 9.1.0, R8 enabled (i.e. a stock `--release` build).

2. flutter build appbundle --release

3. Find the obfuscated name of AccessibilityBridge and its synthetic lambdas in
   build/app/outputs/mapping/release/mapping.txt:

     io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge -> io.flutter.view.a
     io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge$$ExternalSyntheticLambda1 -> t2

4. Extract the DEX from the AAB and disassemble the constructor:

     dexdump -d classes4.dex   # the DEX containing io.flutter.view.a

   Observe in AccessibilityBridge.<init>:

     sget          v0, Landroid/os/Build$VERSION;.SDK_INT:I
     const/16      v1, #int 34
     if-lt         v0, v1, 0040
     003a: new-instance  v0, Lt2;        <-- API-34 lambda, never executes below 34
     0040: new-instance  v0, Ll;         <-- the no-op lambda
     0045: iput-object   v0, v2, Lio/flutter/view/a;.<field>:Lb3;   <-- the type join

   Lt2; declares Landroid/app/UiModeManager$ContrastChangeListener; (API 34) and has
   onContrastChanged(F)V. No stub for that interface exists in any DEX in the bundle.

5. Run that build on a pre-34 device whose ART eagerly resolves the type join at 0045.
   The app dies at launch. Not every pre-34 device does this - most ART builds tolerate the
   unresolved join - which is why this presents as a small, persistent slice of users rather
   than a universal failure.
```

### Expected results

The app launches. A version-gated branch that never executes on the device should not prevent
io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge from loading, and AccessibilityBridge.<init> should contain
no API-34 types in its verifiable body.

### Actual results

The app cannot launch at all on an affected device. FlutterView.attachToFlutterEngine constructs
AccessibilityBridge unconditionally, so the process dies in Activity.performStart before a single
line of Dart runs. No accessibility service needs to be enabled.

Fatal Exception: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Lt2;
    at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init>(AccessibilityBridge.java:428)
    at io.flutter.view.AccessibilityBridge.<init>(AccessibilityBridge.java:447)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterView.attachToFlutterEngine(FlutterView.java:1225)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterActivityAndFragmentDelegate.onCreateView(...:437)
    at io.flutter.embedding.android.FlutterFragment.onCreateView(FlutterFragment.java:1121)
    at androidx.fragment.app.Fragment.performCreateView(Fragment.java:3115)
    ...
    at android.app.Activity.performStart(Activity.java:8330)
    at android.app.ActivityThread.handleStartActivity(ActivityThread.java:3670)

Caused by java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: t2

Device is Android 12/13 by the frames (Looper.loopOnce:201 / loop:288,
ActivityThread.main:7872, and jdk.internal.misc.Unsafe, which libcore moved to in S).

Mechanism: ART resolves the synthetic while verifying the type join of the ternary's two
branches at the iput-object, even though the if-lt means the API-34 branch never executes. The
superinterface does not exist below API 34, so DexFile.defineClass fails - and because it
swallows the NoClassDefFoundError into `suppressed` and returns null, the loader surfaces it as
ClassNotFoundException.

Seen on four consecutive releases of a production app. `Lt2;` is only R8's name for the
synthetic and varies per build; an earlier release crashed as `Lio/flutter/view/a;` - same
failure, different name.

> The form asks for a `flutter create bug` reproduction. There isn't a Dart-level one: the defect
> is in the engine's Java and manifests only on specific ART builds. Say so explicitly and give the
> engine source instead — that is what a triager needs here.

issues.title: flutter attach has no --flavor, so appFlavor becomes null after hot restart
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Any app with Android product flavors (e.g. `dev`) that reads `appFlavor` from `package:flutter/services.dart`.
2. Build and launch it with the flavor *outside* `flutter run` — e.g. `flutter build apk --flavor dev --debug` + `adb install` + launch, or via an instrumentation test runner.
3. `flutter attach --debug` to the running app.
4. Press `R` (hot restart).

### Expected results

`appFlavor` stays `dev` after hot restart, as it does under `flutter run --flavor dev` since #169298.

### Actual results

`appFlavor` is `dev` before the first hot restart and `null` after it.

`flutter attach` has no `--flavor` option, so `FlutterCommand.getBuildInfo()` resolves `flavor` to `null` and never adds `FLUTTER_APP_FLAVOR` to the dart defines used by the resident compiler. Passing `FLUTTER_APP_FLAVOR` via `--dart-define` or the environment is rejected by the tool by design. The only workaround is a static `default-flavor` in `pubspec.yaml`, which cannot follow a per-invocation flavor.

This is the same class of problem as flutter/flutter-intellij#5217 / #5237, where the IDE "Attach" action failed with `Could not find an option named 'flavor'` and was worked around by dropping the flag.

### Proposed fix

Register `usesFlavorOption()` in `AttachCommand`. `getBuildInfo()` already turns it into the `FLUTTER_APP_FLAVOR` define, so no further plumbing is required. PR to follow.

issues.title: [vector_math] Quaternion.rotate()/rotated() applies the inverse rotation
issues.body:
## Steps to reproduce

```dart
import 'package:vector_math/vector_math_64.dart';

void main() {
  // 90-degree rotation about +Z.
  final q = Quaternion.axisAngle(Vector3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), 1.5707963267948966);
  final v = Vector3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);

  print(q.rotated(v));           // Quaternion.rotate()/rotated()
  print(q.asRotationMatrix().transformed(v.clone())); // same rotation, via matrix
}
```

## Expected results

By the right-hand rule, rotating `(1, 0, 0)` by 90° about `+Z` should give
`(0, 1, 0)`. `Quaternion.asRotationMatrix()` (and `Matrix4.rotationZ`) agree
with this and print `(≈0, 1, 0)`.

## Actual results

`Quaternion.rotate()` / `rotated()` prints `(≈0, -1, 0)` — the *inverse*
rotation.

## Analysis

`Quaternion.rotate()` in both
[`lib/src/vector_math/quaternion.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/core-packages/blob/main/packages/vector_math/lib/src/vector_math/quaternion.dart)
and
[`lib/src/vector_math_64/quaternion.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/core-packages/blob/main/packages/vector_math/lib/src/vector_math_64/quaternion.dart)
computes the sandwich product in the wrong order:

```dart
// this * [v,0] * conjugate(this) is the standard rotation formula, but the
// code instead computes conjugate(this) * [v,0] * this, i.e. the inverse.
```

This means every caller of `Quaternion.rotate()`/`rotated()` in both the
32-bit and 64-bit variants gets vectors rotated by the inverse of the
quaternion they constructed. It also means the existing hardcoded test
expectations in `test/quaternion_test.dart`'s `testQuaternionNormalize()`
encode the buggy (inverted) direction, since they were presumably derived
from this same implementation rather than independently.

## Additional information

Found via a randomized invariant fuzz test that cross-checks
`Quaternion.rotated()` against `Quaternion.asRotationMatrix()` on the same
input vector — the two disagreed on sign for every non-trivial rotation
axis.

I have a fix + regression tests ready and will open a PR referencing this
issue.

## Logs

N/A — pure Dart math bug, not platform/build specific.

Package: `vector_math` (both `vector_math.dart` and `vector_math_64.dart` entry points)

issues.title: [tool] Intermittent `Failed to load "<file>"` — `_Map<String, dynamic>` is not a subtype of `List<dynamic>` — on `flutter test --coverage`; also silently under-counts tests (refiles #190000 with a measured rate)
issues.body:
### Summary

This refiles #190000, which was closed on 2026-08-17 for want of a reproduction and locked on
2026-08-31; its closing message asks for a new issue rather than a comment. Same signature, a
different Flutter version, and three things that report did not have:

1. the `--coverage` code path that makes the implicated machinery reachable at all, traced through
   `flutter_tools`' own source;
2. an occurrence rate measured on a production CI over a defined window, rather than a synthetic loop;
3. a **quantified** measurement of the silent test under-count #190000 noticed, taken from two runs
   of a byte-identical tree.

**I do not have a minimal reproduction either**, and I am saying so up front. What I have is a suite
that hits this several times a week on a machine I control, and an offer at the bottom that follows
from that.

### The failure

Verbatim from a CI job log (`flutter test --coverage --reporter compact`):

```
04:47 +5163 ~2 -1: loading <workspace>/test/sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart [E]
  Failed to load "<workspace>/test/sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart": type '_Map<String, dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'List<dynamic>' in type cast
  dart:_internal/async_cast.dart 80:25          CastStreamSubscription._onData
  dart:async/zone_root.dart 48:47               _rootRunUnary
  dart:async/zone.dart 733:19                   _CustomZone.runUnary
  dart:async/zone.dart 633:7                    _CustomZone.runUnaryGuarded
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 381:11            _BufferingStreamSubscription._sendData
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 312:7             _BufferingStreamSubscription._add
  dart:async/stream_controller.dart 798:19      _SyncStreamControllerDispatch._sendData
  dart:async/stream_controller.dart 663:7       _StreamController._add
  dart:async/stream_controller.dart 618:5       _StreamController.add
  dart:async/zone_root.dart 48:47               _rootRunUnary
  dart:async/zone.dart 733:19                   _CustomZone.runUnary
  dart:async/zone.dart 633:7                    _CustomZone.runUnaryGuarded
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 381:11            _BufferingStreamSubscription._sendData
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 573:14            _DelayedData.perform
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 678:11            _PendingEvents.handleNext
  dart:async/stream_impl.dart 649:7             _PendingEvents.schedule.<fn>
  dart:async/zone_root.dart 27:47               _rootRun
  dart:async/zone.dart 726:19                   _CustomZone.run
  dart:async/zone.dart 625:7                    _CustomZone.runGuarded
  dart:async/zone.dart 666:23                   _CustomZone.bindCallbackGuarded.<fn>
  dart:async/zone_root.dart 35:13               _rootRun
  dart:async/zone.dart 726:19                   _CustomZone.run
  dart:async/zone.dart 625:7                    _CustomZone.runGuarded
  dart:async/zone.dart 666:23                   _CustomZone.bindCallbackGuarded.<fn>
  dart:async/schedule_microtask.dart 40:35      _microtaskLoop
  dart:async/schedule_microtask.dart 49:5       _startMicrotaskLoop
  dart:isolate-patch/isolate_patch.dart 127:13  _runPendingImmediateCallback
  dart:isolate-patch/isolate_patch.dart 194:5   _RawReceivePort._handleMessage
```

**28 stack frames, every one of them `dart:async`, `dart:_internal` or `dart:isolate-patch`, and not
a single user frame** — the trace bottoms out in `_RawReceivePort._handleMessage`, i.e. an incoming
message on the isolate's port, never in anything the file under load did. The run then ends
`05:18 +5747 ~3 -1: Some tests failed.` — one red entry against 5,747 passing.

### The named file is innocent, established four ways

- **It differs every time.** Across the occurrences below the named file spans a repository test, a
  widget test, a stress test, an e2e test and a data test. They share no import beyond
  `package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart` and `package:flutter/material.dart`, which all ~600 files
  in the suite have.
- **Each passes in isolation**, run on the same branch, immediately after.
- **The same commit fails then passes.** `gh run rerun` on a byte-identical tree goes green with no
  code change, repeatedly.
- **One occurrence was on a PR that changed no Dart file at all** (it edited only a generated
  `openapi.json`), so nothing about the code under test can explain a Dart file failing to load.

There is also a trap worth recording, because it cost us a false positive: **`CastStreamSubscription._onData`
is not by itself a signature of this bug.** That frame appears in the `Chain`-formatted trace of *any*
reported failure in a large suite. The only reliable marker is the literal `Failed to load "`.

### Where it throws

#190000 identified this and I can confirm it holds on our pinning (`stream_channel` 2.1.4,
`lib/src/multi_channel.dart:143`):

```dart
_innerStreamSubscription = _inner!.stream.cast<List>().listen((message) {
  var id = (message[0] as num).toInt();
```

A bare `List` in `cast<List>()` is `List<dynamic>` to the VM, which is exactly the type in the
message. Every frame on the inner connection must be `[id, payload]`; a bare JSON object arrived
there instead.

### New: the `--coverage` code path

This is what I think is genuinely new. `--coverage` is not incidental to the configuration — it
changes what is running underneath each test file. Traced in Flutter 3.41.6:

- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart:578` — `collector` is constructed **only** when
  `--coverage`, `--merge-coverage` or `--branch-coverage` is passed.
- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart:684` —
  `enableVmService: collector != null || startPaused || enableVmService,`
- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart:103` vs `:107` — that flag is what
  decides whether each `flutter_tester` subprocess is started with `--vm-service-port=…` or with
  `--disable-vm-service`, making that whole path inert.

So on `--coverage` every test file additionally opens a VM-service/DDS connection, layered on the
per-file reporter channel that `MultiChannel` multiplexes — and `MultiChannel` is precisely where
the cast is.

⚠️ **What this does and does not establish.** It establishes that `--coverage` puts extra machinery
on the same path as the throwing cast. It does **not** establish that `--coverage` is *necessary*:
runs without it looked clean for us, but against a per-run rate this low that sample is badly
underpowered, and I am not going to present it as a control. Treat this as the place to look, not as
a proven precondition.

### New: the rate on a production CI

I swept **every** failed `analyze + test` attempt on our CI over a four-day window
(2026-09-04 → 2026-09-07) and grepped each job log for the literal `Failed to load "`. This includes
attempts on runs that now report *success*, because a re-run passed — those are invisible unless you
go attempt by attempt, which is probably why this kind of rate is rarely reported.

| | |
|---|---|
| Window | 2026-09-04 → 2026-09-07 (4 days) |
| Occurrences (distinct runs) | **22** |
| Files named across them | 23 — one run had **two** files fail to load at once |
| Distinct test files named | **21**; only two were ever named more than once |
| Distinct branches | **14**, of which 8 occurrences were on our trunk |
| Completed suite executions (142 green + 47 red attempts) | 189 |
| **Per-run rate** | **22 / 189 = 11.6%** |
| **Share of all CI failures in the window** | **22 / 47 = 47%** |

Per day: 3, 10, 6, 3.

The last row is the one I would draw attention to: for four days, **roughly half of every CI
failure on this repository was this bug** rather than anything a contributor wrote. The suite is
~5,770 tests over ~600 files, `flutter test --coverage --reporter compact`, default concurrency, on a
dedicated arm64 macOS runner that serialises jobs — so there is no CI-vs-CI overlap to blame.

The 21 file names span every kind of test in the suite — repository, widget, stress, e2e, data,
and (with some irony) a workflow-guard test:

```
pacing_outlier_e2e_test.dart (x2)        analytics_amount_no_truncation_test.dart (x2)
home_refresh_profile_repository_test.dart  home_currency_symbol_test.dart
subscription_detail_stress_test.dart     item_price_map_stale_response_test.dart
register_screen_stress_test.dart         login_screen_stress_test.dart
profile_screen_stress_test.dart          onboarding_first_capture_test.dart
sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart     sync_service_item_rating_test.dart
top_insights_card_test.dart              personal_inflation_slot_test.dart
calendar_heatmap_slot_test.dart          legal_url_scheme_guard_test.dart
integration_workflow_script_guard_test.dart  receipt_item_edit_position_stability_test.dart
product_group_outbox_test.dart           tips_telemetry_uploader_test.dart
dio_factory_test.dart
```

### New: the silent test under-count, quantified

#190000 observed that the run is short by exactly one file's worth of tests and nothing says so
(`+1596` of 1600). Here is the same thing measured against a known-good baseline. Run 34035858305,
two attempts, byte-identical tree:

| attempt | outcome | tests reported passing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | load failure | **5747** (`05:18 +5747 ~3 -1: Some tests failed.`) |
| 2 | green re-run, no code change | **5771** |

**Exactly 24 tests went missing — and `sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart` contains exactly 24
tests. The whole file ran nowhere and was reported nowhere.**
Our CI has a gate that compares the passing-test count against the last known-good count on the base
branch, which is the only reason the discrepancy was visible at all.

I want to argue this half is separately fixable and worth fixing on its own merits, whatever the root
cause turns out to be: a load failure already produces one red entry, so the runner *knows* the file
never ran. Reporting "N tests in this file did not run" — or simply not letting the total silently
shrink — would turn a suite that quietly tests less than it claims into one that says so. That is a
worse failure mode than the confusing message, and it does not depend on anyone reproducing the race.

### Impact

On a single self-hosted runner that serialises jobs, each occurrence costs a full cycle and lands on
a **random** PR, so it reads as that PR's defect. It has blocked a merge on an integration branch
whose own content was entirely unrelated. The expensive property is not the wasted run — it is that
it **camouflages real failures**: once people learn to hit re-run on this signature, they will
eventually re-run past a genuine one. We have already had a run that contained both this and a real
regression at the same time.

### What I can offer

#190000's reporter offered to run an instrumented build and never got a patch to run. I can make the
same offer from a better position: a ~5,770-test suite on a dedicated macOS runner that reproduces
this at the rate above, several times a week, unattended.

**If someone points me at a patch, a debug print in `MultiChannel` / `_pipeHarnessToRemote`, or a
flag combination that would capture the offending message, I will run it in a loop until it fires and
post exactly what comes out.** Catching that one message is what turns this from a symptom into a
cause, and it is the piece nobody has yet.

### Environment

- Flutter **3.41.6** stable, Dart 3.11.4, macOS 26.6.2 arm64.
  (#190000 reported **3.44.7**. Ours is the *older* stable of the two, so the defect spans at
  least 3.41.6 → 3.44.7 and is not a recent regression.)
- `stream_channel` 2.1.4, `test_api` 0.7.10, `vm_service` 15.2.0.
- Command: `flutter test --coverage --reporter compact`, default concurrency, no sharding.

```

**28 stack frames, every one of them `dart:async`, `dart:_internal` or `dart:isolate-patch`, and not
a single user frame** — the trace bottoms out in `_RawReceivePort._handleMessage`, i.e. an incoming
message on the isolate's port, never in anything the file under load did. The run then ends
`05:18 +5747 ~3 -1: Some tests failed.` — one red entry against 5,747 passing.

### The named file is innocent, established four ways

- **It differs every time.** Across the occurrences below the named file spans a repository test, a
  widget test, a stress test, an e2e test and a data test. They share no import beyond
  `package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart` and `package:flutter/material.dart`, which all ~600 files
  in the suite have.
- **Each passes in isolation**, run on the same branch, immediately after.
- **The same commit fails then passes.** `gh run rerun` on a byte-identical tree goes green with no
  code change, repeatedly.
- **One occurrence was on a PR that changed no Dart file at all** (it edited only a generated
  `openapi.json`), so nothing about the code under test can explain a Dart file failing to load.

There is also a trap worth recording, because it cost us a false positive: **`CastStreamSubscription._onData`
is not by itself a signature of this bug.** That frame appears in the `Chain`-formatted trace of *any*
reported failure in a large suite. The only reliable marker is the literal `Failed to load "`.

### Where it throws

 identified this and I can confirm it holds on our pinning (`stream_channel` 2.1.4,
`lib/src/multi_channel.dart:143`):

```dart
_innerStreamSubscription = _inner!.stream.cast<List>().listen((message) {
  var id = (message[0] as num).toInt();
```

A bare `List` in `cast<List>()` is `List<dynamic>` to the VM, which is exactly the type in the
message. Every frame on the inner connection must be `[id, payload]`; a bare JSON object arrived
there instead.

### New: the `--coverage` code path

This is what I think is genuinely new. `--coverage` is not incidental to the configuration — it
changes what is running underneath each test file. Traced in Flutter 3.41.6:

- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart:578` — `collector` is constructed **only** when
  `--coverage`, `--merge-coverage` or `--branch-coverage` is passed.
- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/test.dart:684` —
  `enableVmService: collector != null || startPaused || enableVmService,`
- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/test/flutter_tester_device.dart:103` vs `:107` — that flag is what
  decides whether each `flutter_tester` subprocess is started with `--vm-service-port=…` or with
  `--disable-vm-service`, making that whole path inert.

So on `--coverage` every test file additionally opens a VM-service/DDS connection, layered on the
per-file reporter channel that `MultiChannel` multiplexes — and `MultiChannel` is precisely where
the cast is.

⚠️ **What this does and does not establish.** It establishes that `--coverage` puts extra machinery
on the same path as the throwing cast. It does **not** establish that `--coverage` is *necessary*:
runs without it looked clean for us, but against a per-run rate this low that sample is badly
underpowered, and I am not going to present it as a control. Treat this as the place to look, not as
a proven precondition.

### New: the rate on a production CI

I swept **every** failed `analyze + test` attempt on our CI over a four-day window
(2026-09-04 → 2026-09-07) and grepped each job log for the literal `Failed to load "`. This includes
attempts on runs that now report *success*, because a re-run passed — those are invisible unless you
go attempt by attempt, which is probably why this kind of rate is rarely reported.

| | |
|---|---|
| Window | 2026-09-04 → 2026-09-07 (4 days) |
| Occurrences (distinct runs) | **22** |
| Files named across them | 23 — one run had **two** files fail to load at once |
| Distinct test files named | **21**; only two were ever named more than once |
| Distinct branches | **14**, of which 8 occurrences were on our trunk |
| Completed suite executions (142 green + 47 red attempts) | 189 |
| **Per-run rate** | **22 / 189 = 11.6%** |
| **Share of all CI failures in the window** | **22 / 47 = 47%** |

Per day: 3, 10, 6, 3.

The last row is the one I would draw attention to: for four days, **roughly half of every CI
failure on this repository was this bug** rather than anything a contributor wrote. The suite is
~5,770 tests over ~600 files, `flutter test --coverage --reporter compact`, default concurrency, on a
dedicated arm64 macOS runner that serialises jobs — so there is no CI-vs-CI overlap to blame.

The 21 file names span every kind of test in the suite — repository, widget, stress, e2e, data,
and (with some irony) a workflow-guard test:

```
pacing_outlier_e2e_test.dart (x2)        analytics_amount_no_truncation_test.dart (x2)
home_refresh_profile_repository_test.dart  home_currency_symbol_test.dart
subscription_detail_stress_test.dart     item_price_map_stale_response_test.dart
register_screen_stress_test.dart         login_screen_stress_test.dart
profile_screen_stress_test.dart          onboarding_first_capture_test.dart
sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart     sync_service_item_rating_test.dart
top_insights_card_test.dart              personal_inflation_slot_test.dart
calendar_heatmap_slot_test.dart          legal_url_scheme_guard_test.dart
integration_workflow_script_guard_test.dart  receipt_item_edit_position_stability_test.dart
product_group_outbox_test.dart           tips_telemetry_uploader_test.dart
dio_factory_test.dart
```

### New: the silent test under-count, quantified

 observed that the run is short by exactly one file's worth of tests and nothing says so
(`+1596` of 1600). Here is the same thing measured against a known-good baseline. Run 34035858305,
two attempts, byte-identical tree:

| attempt | outcome | tests reported passing |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | load failure | **5747** (`05:18 +5747 ~3 -1: Some tests failed.`) |
| 2 | green re-run, no code change | **5771** |

**Exactly 24 tests went missing — and `sync_service_item_favorite_test.dart` contains exactly 24
tests. The whole file ran nowhere and was reported nowhere.**
Our CI has a gate that compares the passing-test count against the last known-good count on the base
branch, which is the only reason the discrepancy was visible at all.

I want to argue this half is separately fixable and worth fixing on its own merits, whatever the root
cause turns out to be: a load failure already produces one red entry, so the runner *knows* the file
never ran. Reporting "N tests in this file did not run" — or simply not letting the total silently
shrink — would turn a suite that quietly tests less than it claims into one that says so. That is a
worse failure mode than the confusing message, and it does not depend on anyone reproducing the race.

### Impact

On a single self-hosted runner that serialises jobs, each occurrence costs a full cycle and lands on
a **random** PR, so it reads as that PR's defect. It has blocked a merge on an integration branch
whose own content was entirely unrelated. The expensive property is not the wasted run — it is that
it **camouflages real failures**: once people learn to hit re-run on this signature, they will
eventually re-run past a genuine one. We have already had a run that contained both this and a real
regression at the same time.

### What I can offer

's reporter offered to run an instrumented build and never got a patch to run. I can make the
same offer from a better position: a ~5,770-test suite on a dedicated macOS runner that reproduces
this at the rate above, several times a week, unattended.

**If someone points me at a patch, a debug print in `MultiChannel` / `_pipeHarnessToRemote`, or a
flag combination that would capture the offending message, I will run it in a loop until it fires and
post exactly what comes out.** Catching that one message is what turns this from a symptom into a
cause, and it is the piece nobody has yet.

### Environment

- Flutter **3.41.6** stable, Dart 3.11.4, macOS 26.6.2 arm64.
  ( reported **3.44.7**. Ours is the *older* stable of the two, so the defect spans at
  least 3.41.6 → 3.44.7 and is not a recent regression.)
- `stream_channel` 2.1.4, `test_api` 0.7.10, `vm_service` 15.2.0.
- Command: `flutter test --coverage --reporter compact`, default concurrency, no sharding.

issues.title: iOS 26: EXC_BAD_ACCESS in dart::OSThreadPtr::~OSThreadPtr TLS destructor on exiting Dart worker (regression from dart-lang/sdk 1d0195cad4, still present in 3.47.2)
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

No deterministic repro. Production-only crash cluster from App Store (AOT release) builds, reported via our crash reporter. All events share the same trigger: the app starts an `AVAudioEngine` input-tap microphone stream (`record_ios` 2.1.1), and the crash fires 4–5 s later on an unnamed exiting thread — consistent with a Dart VM thread-pool worker exiting after its idle timeout.

1. iOS 26.5.2 / 26.6 / 26.6.1 physical device (iPhone14,4 · iPhone15,2 · iPhone18,1)
2. Start an `AVAudioEngine`-based recorder
3. Wait ~5 s

### Expected results

A VM thread-pool worker exits cleanly.

### Actual results

`EXC_BAD_ACCESS` (mach, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS`, code 1, fatal) during `_pthread_tsd_cleanup`. Crashed thread (from our crash reporter; engine dSYM not uploaded so the three Flutter.framework frames resolve to the nearest exported symbol):

```
_pthread_start
_pthread_exit
_pthread_tsd_cleanup
dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::finalizeList
dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::finalizeList
InternalFlutterGpu_Texture_AsImage   ← misattributed; see below
InternalFlutterGpu_Texture_AsImage
InternalFlutterGpu_Texture_AsImage
```

Fault addresses across 8 events all sit in the same band: `0x10117990560`, `0x1011c996d50`, `0x10121425130`, `0x1012513d880`, `0x1011021f560`, `0x10121cc4dd0`, `0x1014d6755b0`, `0x101106d0d40`.

This is the same signature as #190021 / #190023 (both auto-closed and locked). In the 3.44.4 engine `Flutter.framework.dSYM` (UUID `4C4C4482-5555-3144-A189-47CFFBA6D499`), `dart::OSThreadPtr::~OSThreadPtr`, `dart::OSThread::~OSThread` and `dart::Log::~Log` are all located after the last exported function symbol (`_InternalFlutterGpu_Texture_AsImage` @ 0x518df0), which is why the frames collapse onto that name.

### Regression pointer

The `thread_local OSThreadPtr` destructor path was introduced by dart-lang/sdk commit `1d0195cad4` ("[vm] Use C++11 thread_local for TLS destructors", 2026-03-25), first shipped in Dart 3.12.0 / Flutter 3.44.0. The Dart revisions pinned by Flutter 3.41.9 and 3.38.10 still use the pthread-key destructor. `runtime/vm/os_thread.cc` and `os_thread_macos.cc` are byte-identical between the Dart revisions pinned by Flutter 3.44.4 and 3.47.2, and there are no commits to those files after the revision pinned by 3.44.4, so upgrading does not change the code path.

On iOS 26 the C++ `thread_local` destructors are run by dyld (`dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::finalizeList`) from `_pthread_tsd_cleanup`; the fault happens inside `OSThread::~OSThread` → `delete log_` (`Log::~Log` / `MallocGrowableArray` teardown).

### Data

| | |
|---|---|
| Events | 8 (4 users, 3 device models), 2026-08-21 → 2026-09-05 |
| iOS | 26.6 ×1, 26.5.2 ×4, 26.6.1 ×3 — none on iOS 18 |
| Flutter | 3.44.4 stable, engine a10d8ac38d, Dart 3.12.2 |
| Build | App Store release, `--obfuscate --split-debug-info` |
| Threads alive at crash | io.flutter.1.raster / io.flutter.1.io / io.worker.1–3 / dart:io EventHandler / 4× DartWorker / CoreAudio (`caulk.*`) |

Full crash report (app symbols stripped, Flutter frames symbolicated against the 3.44.4 engine dSYM): https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/192369#issuecomment-5570034537

### Code sample

Not applicable — no app frames on the crashed thread. Relevant plugins: `record` 7.1.1 / `record_ios` 2.1.1, `audio_session` 0.2.4.

### Flutter Doctor output

```
