issues.title: [in_app_purchase_storekit] StoreKit2 finish() never calls completion when the transaction is not found, so completePurchase() hangs forever (incomplete fix for #160148)
flutter test on a physical iOS device hangs ~60s on the 2nd+ integration_test file due to stale mDNS cache in MDnsVmServiceDiscovery
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Have an `integration_test/` directory with 2 or more test files.
2. Connect a physical iOS device (reproduced on iOS 26).
3. Run `flutter test integration_test -d <device-id>` (passing the whole directory, not a single file).

### Expected results

Each test file's app launch discovers the Dart VM Service quickly (sub-second), as happens for the first file.

### Actual results

The **first** file's VM Service is discovered almost instantly. Every **subsequent** file in the same `flutter test` invocation hangs for ~55-60 seconds at "Checking for advertised Dart VM Services...", eventually printing:

```
The Dart VM Service was not discovered after 60 seconds. This is taking much longer than expected...
```

...right after which the service *is* found and the run continues. So it's not a permanent hang, but a consistent ~60s delay per file after the first.

**Control experiment:** Running the exact same two files as two *separate* `flutter test <file> -d <device-id>` invocations, each discovers the VM Service in well under a second. The delay only appears when multiple files run inside the *same* `flutter test` process.

### Suspected root cause

`MDnsVmServiceDiscovery` in [`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/mdns_discovery.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/mdns_discovery.dart) is instantiated once per `flutter_tools` process and reuses the same `MDnsClient` (`_client`) across all test files/app launches within one `flutter test <directory>` invocation. issues.title: ☂️ Convert 1P Swift plugins to Pigeon's `async` support
issues.body:
Pigeon recently (in version 28) added support for the Swift generator to generate `async` functions instead of callback-based functions. That should be adopted across all 1P plugins, for several reasons:
- Using Pigeon functionality in our own plugins has historically been the best way to find issues and areas for improvement, and this is the default generation mode now so we should eat our own dogfood. (Case in point, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/192199, which needs to be fixed before this is adopted for plugins using `FlutterApi`.)
- Our plugins are often examples used by other developers, so using the default mode will make them more useful to the community (and to AI model training).
- `async` functions are not only more idiomatic in modern Swift, but they are safer. We have consistently over the years found issues (https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/192400 is a recent example) where some codepath doesn't call the completion handler exactly one time (usually it's a missing call, but occasionally it's twice), which violates the engine's API contract and causes usually-serious bugs. With an async method, that can't happen
- The FFI backend for Pigeon uses `async`, so adopting it for the current method channel backend will simplify later transitions to FFI.

issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

I don't have great steps to reproduce, it's somewhat inconsistent and I can only repo on GH Actions and in a local container (with a wonky setup).

I'm running Dart-Code's E2E Playwright tests that try to verify the widget preview, and sometimes it crashes.

Logs look approximately like:

```console
    [Info] Spawning flutter with args ["widget-preview","start","--machine","--web-server",...]
    [Info] <== widget_preview.initializing
    [Info] "Launching analysis server..."
    [warning] "Lost connection to the Dart Tooling Daemon (DTD). Live preview updates are paused.
      Details: JSON-RPC error 103: Stream already subscribed"
    [Info] "Launching the Widget Preview Scaffold on Web Server..."
    [Info] "Launching lib/main.dart on Web Server in debug mode..."
    [Info] "Triggering reload..." x3 (all in the same second)
    [error] "Flutter failed to read file at /tmp/flutter_tools.XXX/web_entrypoint.dart.
      PathNotFoundException ... errno 2"
    [Error] Process flutter/bin/flutter terminated! 1
    [Error] Widget Preview server process terminated
```

Looking in [dtd_services](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/widget_preview/dtd_services.dart) my suspicion is a race condition in calls to `_waitForLspService()` being called twice:

1. First by `getFlutterWidgetPreviews()` as the preview starts loading
2. Next by `getFlutterWidgetPreviewsForFile()` as a file is opened

`_waitForLspService` bails out if `_lspServiceAvailable` is already set. However it's set after ` await _dtd!.streamListen(kServiceStream);`. This means if two calls to this function occur at the same time, both could call `streamListen()`.

@bkonyi WDYT, does this sound plausible? I haven't fully debugged this yet, because I can only repro it in containers on remote machines, but I'll try to hack in some logging to verify if that's what's happening.

No crash :)

### Actual results

Process crashes.

issues.title: Proposal: populate MediaQuery.displayFeatures on iOS for iPhone Duo (foldable)
issues.body:
### Use case

Apple announced **iPhone Duo** on September 9, 2026 — the first foldable iPhone, with a 5.4" outer display and a 7.6" inner display that curves through the centre when partially folded. It ships October 23, 2026.

Flutter apps run on it today, but they have **no fold awareness at all**:

- [`DisplayFeature`](https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/dart-ui/DisplayFeature-class.html) is documented as *"populated only on Android."* On iPhone Duo, `MediaQuery.displayFeatures` returns an empty list no matter how folded the device is.
- [`dual_screen`](https://pub.dev/packages/dual_screen) (`TwoPane`, `hingeAngleEvents`) is Android-only in practice and was last published roughly three years ago.

So a Flutter app cannot tell that content or a touch target has landed in the fold — where, on this device, it becomes noticeably harder to read and to tap.

Some of the impact is already solvable in pure Dart, and I don't think Flutter needs to do anything about that part: resizing is handled by `LayoutBuilder`, and the asymmetric safe area (iOS moves its system controls to **one side** on this device) is correctly reported through `MediaQuery.paddingOf` per edge. That covers a good portion of a decent port.

What is *not* reachable from Dart is the fold itself, and the under-display camera region.

**Alternatives considered.** Each app can write its own platform channel to the new iOS APIs. That works — but it means every foldable-aware Flutter app reimplements the same bridge, and none of them feed `MediaQuery.displayFeatures`, so no existing display-feature-aware widget or package benefits. Given `DisplayFeature` already exists as the platform-neutral abstraction, populating it on iOS seems strictly better than N private channels.

Related: #189554 proposes built-in split-view/dual-pane support for large screens and foldables. This issue is narrower — just getting the platform data into `dart:ui`.

### Proposal

Populate `DisplayFeature` on iOS from the reserved-region APIs introduced in iOS 27.1, in the Darwin embedder (`engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/ios/`), plumbed through `ViewportMetrics` the same way the Android embedder does it from Jetpack WindowManager.

iOS 27.1 adds `reservedRegions(kind:)` on `UIView`, returning regions with a `frame`, a kind, and an active/inactive state:

- **`.division`** — an area that splits a larger area into smaller ones. The fold is a division region. It is *active* only while the device is folded; flat, it is inactive with zero width.
- **`.occlusion`** — an area that covers part of the view without splitting it. The under-display FaceTime camera on the inner display is an occlusion region, active only while that camera is in use.
- A query option `includeInactive` returns regions that exist but are not currently active.

A mapping onto the existing model that I think holds up:

| iOS 27.1 reserved region | `DisplayFeatureType` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.division` (the fold) | `fold` | Flutter defines `fold` as *not obstructing* the display and `hinge` as obstructing. iPhone Duo's inner display is a single continuous panel that curves — there is no gap and no second panel — so `fold` is the accurate value and `hinge` would be misleading. |
| `.occlusion` (under-display camera) | `cutout` | Occludes without dividing, which matches `cutout` semantics. |

| iOS region state | `DisplayFeatureState` |
|---|---|
| active | `postureHalfOpened` |
| inactive (zero width when flat) | `postureFlat` |

`bounds` maps directly from the region's frame, converted to logical pixels.

#### One open design question

**Flutter has no equivalent of `includeInactive`, and I think that gap is worth deciding on deliberately rather than by omission.**

On iOS you can ask "does this device *have* a fold, even though it is flat right now?" That is genuinely useful for stable layout decisions — Apple's guidance gives the example of always preferring an even number of grid columns on a device that has a fold, so the layout does not reshuffle every time the user bends it.

Flutter's model cannot express that: an inactive feature simply is not in the list, so `displayFeatures` is empty on a flat iPhone Duo and equally empty on an iPhone 18. An app that wants to lay out stably across the fold cannot distinguish them.

Possible directions, roughly in order of invasiveness:

1. Report the inactive fold as a `DisplayFeature` with `state: postureFlat` and zero-width bounds — arguably already consistent with `postureFlat` existing at all, and requires no API change.
2. Add an opt-in accessor for inactive features.
3. Leave it out for now, and document that `displayFeatures` reflects only currently-active features.

Option 1 looks cheapest and most useful to me, but it is a behavioural decision for the team — it would mean a flat foldable reports a feature where today it would report none, and that could surprise Android callers.

#### Caveat on my end

I have not been able to verify these iOS API signatures against the SDK. iPhone Duo was announced on September 9 and Xcode 27.1 was still rolling out at the time of writing, so everything above comes from Apple's Tech Talk sessions rather than shipped headers. I would treat the names as *the shape of the API* and confirm against the SDK before implementing.

I am filing this as a proposal rather than a PR for that reason — I cannot build or test the engine change, so I did not want to submit code I could not verify. Happy to help with documentation or follow-up detail if that is useful.

Primary sources (Apple):

- [Get ready for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/iphone-duo/)
- [Strike a pose with adaptive layouts on iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111463/) — reserved regions, division vs occlusion, `includeInactive`
- [Prepare your app for iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111461/) — asymmetric safe areas, size classes
- [Leverage multiple displays and scenes on iPhone Duo](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111464/) — hinge angle (`UIHingeInteraction`), out of scope here but related
- [Apple unveils iPhone Duo](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-unveils-iphone-duo/) — device specifications

issues.title: [widget_previews] Intercept prohibited hot reloads and hot restart instead
issues.body:
### Use case

When using widget previews using `flutter widget-preview start` and hot reload is prohibited, the widget previewer should try hot restarting instead, since we cannot do it ourselves, since we do not control stdin for the previewer process.

### Proposal

Have the widget previewer intercept messages such as

```
Exception: Const class cannot remove fields: Library:'package:my_project/foo/bar.dart' Class: Bar
Hot reload rejected due to unsupported changes. Try performing a hot restart instead.
```

log that a hot reload was prevented and that a hot restart will be done instead.

issues.title: [widget_previews] [Proposal] Consider providing better errors if widget preview is unconstrained
issues.model_input:
Title: [widget_previews] [Proposal] Consider providing better errors if widget preview is unconstrained

Description:
### Use case

People writing widget previews, that accidentally forget that a preview needs a fixed size constraint.

For example:

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widget_previews.dart';
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

@Preview(name: 'Oops')
Widget buildPreview() => const Foo();

class Foo extends StatelessWidget {
  const Foo();

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SizedBox.expand(child: Text('Oops'));
  }
}
```

Then you get something like this in stdout of the widget previewer

```
The following RenderObject was being processed when the exception was fired: RenderConstrainedBox#f9f73 relayoutBoundary=up58 NEEDS-LAYOUT NEEDS-PAINT NEEDS-COMPOSITING-BITS-UPDATE:
  creator: SizedBox ← Foo ← @Preview ← EnableWidgetInspectorScope ←
    WidgetPreviewTheming ← Container-[GlobalKey#9acff] ← ValueListenableBuilder<bool> ← SizedBox ←
    _WidgetPreviewWrapper ← ValueListenableBuilder<bool> ← MediaQuery ←
    ValueListenableBuilder<Brightness> ← ⋯
  parentData: <none> (can use size)
  constraints: BoxConstraints(unconstrained)
  size: MISSING
  additionalConstraints: BoxConstraints(w=Infinity, h=34.0)
```

### Proposal

Consider intercepting errors that indicate an unconstrained size and fail with a descriptive message.

For example the following is a red flag about the unconstrained layout

```
  constraints: BoxConstraints(unconstrained)
  size: MISSING
  additionalConstraints: BoxConstraints(w=Infinity, h=34.0)
```

issues.title: [tool][iOS][macOS] Renamed Xcode projects still use hardcoded Runner paths for host files, plugin registration, and migrations
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

I am facing the issue for several years and use local fix to support. Some of the following conslusions are investigated by AI.

Related discussion: [flutter/flutter#9767](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/9767#issuecomment-1533771721). [PR #124533](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/124533) added discovery of renamed `.xcodeproj` and `.xcworkspace` directories. The [maintainer discussion](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/124533#issuecomment-1517204572) explicitly limited that change to those containers; source-directory and scheme renaming were deferred. This report concerns the remaining host-file discovery gap and its effects on newer tooling, including UIScene migration, rather than a regression of that fix.

The following reproduction procedure is proposed from source inspection; an unpatched-SDK execution log and standalone sample still need to be attached.

1. Create a Flutter application with iOS and macOS support and add a plugin that requires an iOS plugin registrant.
2. Rename the native Xcode project, workspace, application target, and on-disk host source directory from `Runner` to `Hello`. Update Xcode file references, build settings, workspace/scheme references, bridging-header paths, and CocoaPods project/target references as applicable. Keep the shared scheme named `Runner` to isolate file discovery from scheme-selection behavior.
3. Verify that Xcode references `Hello/Info.plist`, `Hello/AppDelegate.swift`, and the plugin registrant under `Hello/`, with no stale `Runner/` source references.
4. Run `flutter pub get -v` with an unmodified Flutter SDK and inspect where the iOS `GeneratedPluginRegistrant.h/.m` files are generated.  They are generated under `Runner` (new created empty folder with these 2 GeneratedPluginRegistrant files only) 

Project/target/source-directory names and scheme names are independent. The affected real application uses `Hello.xcodeproj`, the `Hello` target, and `Hello/` source directories, while retaining `Runner.xcscheme` on both platforms.



### Expected results

After valid native project references are updated, Flutter should consistently locate the selected application's Info.plist, AppDelegate, and generated plugin registrant destination. Eligible migrations should operate on those resolved files.

Renaming alone should not make existing host files appear missing. If a layout cannot be resolved safely, the tool should identify the unresolved file and selected target and provide actionable guidance. Custom AppDelegate contents should retain the existing manual-migration safeguards.


### Actual results

Source inspection of Flutter **3.47.4**, revision `9584c6713b324636289d067944a46fd6b49df14b`, shows that project-container discovery and host-file discovery use inconsistent assumptions. The SDK has local changes; the baseline behavior below was checked against its Git diff.

In [`xcode_project.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9584c6713b324636289d067944a46fd6b49df14b/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/xcode_project.dart):

| Accessor | Baseline assumption | Effect with a renamed source directory or target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hostAppProjectName` / `xcodeProject` | Discover the `.xcodeproj` basename | Correctly recognize `Hello.xcodeproj` |
| `defaultHostInfoPlist` | `<platform>/Runner/Info.plist` | Misses the real `Hello/Info.plist` on iOS and macOS |
| iOS `appDelegateSwift`, `appDelegateObjcImplementation`, `appDelegateObjcHeader`, `infoPlist` | Files under `Runner/` | Miss renamed host files; `isSwift` also depends on the misplaced Swift delegate lookup |
| iOS `pluginRegistrantHost` for non-module apps | `ios/Runner/` | Registrant generation targets a directory different from the one referenced by the renamed application |
| macOS `appDelegateSwift` | `macos/Runner/AppDelegate.swift` | AppDelegate migrations cannot locate the renamed file |
| `podRunnerTargetSupportFiles`, `podRunnerFrameworksScript` | `Pods-Runner` and `Pods-Runner-frameworks.sh` | CocoaPods migrations can miss support files for a renamed target |
| `xcodeProjectSchemeFile()` without an explicit scheme | `Runner.xcscheme` | Additional limitation if the scheme is renamed; not the trigger in the example above |

The [iOS registrant writer](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9584c6713b324636289d067944a46fd6b49df14b/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/flutter_plugins.dart) consumes these registrant accessors. This can leave the registrant referenced by the application missing or stale while generating files under `ios/Runner/`. Exact build errors depend on the existing generated files and project references.

The [UIScene migration](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9584c6713b324636289d067944a46fd6b49df14b/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/migrations/uiscene_migration.dart) first checks `defaultHostInfoPlist`. If the hardcoded path does not exist, it emits a missing-plist trace and manual-migration guidance. Correcting only that accessor is insufficient: the next stage still uses the hardcoded AppDelegate accessors. For an eligible renamed project, it can then report that AppDelegate cannot be found.

Other consumers include the iOS `@main` migration, macOS `@main` and secure-restorable-state migrations, and CocoaPods script migrations. Their applicability depends on the project's contents; this report does not claim every migration fails on every renamed app.


### Code sample

This is my local change to fix the issue for several years. Not including all fixes though.

```dart
--- a/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/xcode_project.dart
+++ b/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/xcode_project.dart
@@ -94,7 +94,7 @@ abstract class XcodeBasedProject extends FlutterProjectPlatform {
 
   /// The default 'Info.plist' file of the host app. The developer can change this location in Xcode.
   File get defaultHostInfoPlist =>
-      hostAppRoot.childDirectory(_defaultHostAppName).childFile('Info.plist');
+      hostAppRoot.childDirectory(hostAppProjectName).childFile('Info.plist');
 
   /// The Xcode project (.xcodeproj directory) of the host app.
   Directory get xcodeProject => hostAppRoot.childDirectory('$hostAppProjectName.xcodeproj');
@@ -959,7 +959,7 @@ def __lldb_init_module(debugger: lldb.SBDebugger, _):
     if (productName == null) {
       globals.printTrace('$kProductNameKey not present, defaulting to $hostAppProjectName');
     }
-    return productName ?? XcodeBasedProject._defaultHostAppName;
+    return productName ?? '$hostAppProjectName.app';
   }
 
   Future<void> ensureReadyForPlatformSpecificTooling() async {
@@ -1147,7 +1147,7 @@ def __lldb_init_module(debugger: lldb.SBDebugger, _):
   Directory get pluginRegistrantHost {
     return isModule
         ? _flutterLibRoot.childDirectory('Flutter').childDirectory('FlutterPluginRegistrant')
-        : hostAppRoot.childDirectory(XcodeBasedProject._defaultHostAppName);
+        : hostAppRoot.childDirectory(hostAppProjectName);
   }
```


### Screenshots or Video

Not applicable; this is a file-resolution/tooling issue.


### Logs

Not applicable

issues.title: Delete `Mac mac_unopt > ci/ios_debug_unopt_sim`
issues.body:
Currently we have `Mac mac_unopt > ci/ios_debug_unopt_sim`, but we also have `Mac mac_unopt > ci/ios_debug_unopt_sim_arm64`

The non-arm version of the test verifies that an x86 build of the engine works on a simulator.

Xcode no longer supports intel simulators and is dropping Rosetta support. We should just remove this build. The x86 simulator build will still be built in `Mac mac_ios_engine > ci/ios_debug_sim`, we're just not going to test it anymore.

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1ceffd11a4714c13566358ba4a7b72b7915805bb/engine/src/flutter/ci/builders/mac_unopt.json#L266-L330

issues.title: [Devicelab] ios_add2app_uiscene README still references renamed module_uiscene_test_ios task
issues.body:
### Description

[`dev/integration_tests/ios_add2app_uiscene/README.md`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/dev/integration_tests/ios_add2app_uiscene/README.md) has not been updated since it was created in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/175866 (2025-09-29). It has since drifted out of date in two independent ways.

### 1. Stale task name (regression from #192173)

`module_uiscene_test_ios` was renamed to `uiscene_plugin_lifecycle_test_ios` in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192173, but the README was not updated. The documented commands therefore fail, because no task by that name exists:

```bash
../../bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart bin/test_runner.dart test -t module_uiscene_test_ios
```

| Line | Content |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | ``The test is located at `dev/devicelab/bin/tasks/module_uiscene_test_ios.dart`.`` |
| 32 | `... test -t module_uiscene_test_ios` |
| 38 | `... test -t module_uiscene_test_ios --local-engine <your_local_engine> --local-engine-host host_debug` |
| 44 | `... test -t module_uiscene_test_ios --task-args destination=[/path/to/copy/destination]` |
| 49 | ``... the `scenarios` map in the `Scenarios` class in `dev/devicelab/bin/tasks/module_uiscene_test_ios.dart`.`` |



### 2. Incomplete Purpose section (pre-existing, unrelated to #192173)

Separately, the **Purpose** section (lines 9-16) documents only the four original app/plugin migration permutations. Scenario groups added over the past year are undocumented. 

| Scenario group | Added in |
| --- | --- |
| `AppMigrated-FlutterSceneLifeCycleProvider-*` | #175866 | 
| `AppMigrated-StateRestoration` / `AppNotMigrated-StateRestoration` | #176635 |

issues.title: flutter test integration_test on Android uninstalls the installed app even when the Gradle build fails
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms android bug` and `cd bug`
2. Add `integration_test` to `dev_dependencies` in `pubspec.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   dev_dependencies:
     integration_test:
       sdk: flutter
   ```
3. Create `integration_test/app_test.dart` with the code sample below. It contains a deliberate compile error, so the build of the test fails.
4. Install the app normally and give it some data:
   ```
   flutter build apk --debug
   adb -s emulator-5554 install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell run-as com.example.bug sh -c "'mkdir -p files && echo user-data > files/data.txt'"
   adb -s emulator-5554 shell run-as com.example.bug cat files/data.txt   # prints: user-data
   ```
5. `flutter test integration_test/app_test.dart -d emulator-5554 --verbose`
6. `adb -s emulator-5554 shell pm list packages com.example.bug`

### Expected results

The Gradle build fails, so nothing is installed and no test runs. `flutter test` should report the build failure and leave the device as it found it. The app installed in step 4, and its data, should still be there.

At most, it would be reasonable to uninstall a package that this run actually installed. Here it installed nothing.

### Actual results

The build fails (`Execution failed for task ':app:compileFlutterBuildDebug'`, `Gradle task assembleDebug failed with exit code 1`). During cleanup, `flutter test` then runs:

```
adb -s emulator-5554 shell am force-stop com.example.bug
adb -s emulator-5554 uninstall com.example.bug
```

`pm list packages com.example.bug` prints nothing afterwards, and `run-as com.example.bug cat files/data.txt` fails with `run-as: unknown package: com.example.bug`. *The app installed before the run, and all of its data, are deleted by a test run that never installed anything.* 😬

Where it happens (Flutter 3.47.2, paths in `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/`):

- `test/integration_test_device.dart:50` resolves `_applicationPackage` before `device.startApp(...)`, which is where the Gradle build runs (`:59`).
- `test/flutter_platform.dart` registers a finalizer that calls `testDevice.kill()` whether or not `start()` succeeded.
- `kill()` (`integration_test_device.dart:143-153`) calls `stopApp` and, unless `--no-uninstall` is given, `uninstallApp` on that pre-resolved package. It never checks whether this run installed it. 😬🤦‍♂️

Passing `--no-uninstall` avoids the uninstall; the force-stop still happens.

`flutter drive` handles the same failure safely. 👍 The `ToolExit` from the build propagates out of `DriverService.start` and `stop()` is never reached, so nothing is uninstalled (verified with the same broken test).

Related: #88690. The package resolved before the build can also be the wrong id, e.g. the `namespace` when the build uses `applicationIdSuffix` or a flavor. In that case, uninstalling after a failed build removes whichever app owns the base id.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

`integration_test/app_test.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:integration_test/integration_test.dart';

void main() {
  IntegrationTestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  // Deliberate compile error, so the Gradle build of this test fails.
  final int broken = 'not an int';

  testWidgets('never runs', (tester) async {
    expect(broken, 0);
  });
}
```

Everything else is the unmodified `flutter create --platforms android bug` template, plus `integration_test` in `dev_dependencies`.

issues.title: iOS: Shared `ContextMTL` gpu state relies on a switch that can outlive its owning engine/shell in a `FlutterEngineGroup`
issues.body:
In a `FlutterEngineGroup`, all engines share a single `IOSContext`, and therefore a single Impeller `ContextMTL`, but each engine's `Shell` has its own `fml::SyncSwitch` for GPU availability. The shared `ContextMTL` registers its GPU-availability observer against the switch belonging to whichever engine's `PlatformViewIOS` happened to construct the `IOSContext`.

That engine can be deallocated while further spawned child engines live on. On shutdown that engine's Shell's switch object survives (it's a `std::shared_ptr` and the context is holding on to it, but since it no longer has a Shell owner, nothing can ever write to it again, so it gets frozen at its last value and the shared context stops receiving GPU-availability notifications for the remaining lifetime of the process.

## How we can end up in this state

There are two different `PlatformViewIOS` constructors involved:

| Path | Constructor | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| First engine | `PlatformViewIOS(delegate, controller, task_runners, is_gpu_disabled_sync_switch)` | Calls `IOSContext::Create(switch, …)`, creating the context and binding the observer to that shell's switch |
| Spawned engine | `PlatformViewIOS(delegate, context, controller, task_runners)` | Adopts the spawner's `IOSContext`; takes no switch at all |

Meanwhile every `Shell` unconditionally constructs its own switch:

```cpp
// shell/common/shell.cc
is_gpu_disabled_sync_switch_(new fml::SyncSwitch(is_gpu_disabled)),
```

So an N-engine group has N shells, N switches, N platform views, but one `IOSContext`, one `FlutterDarwinContextMetalImpeller`, one `ContextMTL`, one `AiksContext`.

Ownership chain:

```
PlatformViewIOS
  └── std::shared_ptr<IOSContext> ios_context_            <- shared across the group
        └── IOSContextMetalImpeller
              └── FlutterDarwinContextMetalImpeller*
                    └── std::shared_ptr<impeller::ContextMTL>
                          └── shared_ptr<const fml::SyncSwitch> + registered Observer
```

## API inconsistency/assymmetry

`SnapshotControllerImpeller::MakeImpellerSnapshot` decides whether to defer work using **its own** shell's switch, but parks the deferred task on the **shared** context:

```cpp
// shell/common/snapshot_controller_impeller.cc
std::shared_ptr<const fml::SyncSwitch> sync_switch =
    GetDelegate().GetIsGpuDisabledSyncSwitch();     // this engine's Shell switch
sync_switch->Execute(
    fml::SyncSwitch::Handlers()
        .SetIfTrue([&] {
          ...
          context->GetContext()->StoreTaskForGPU(...);   // SHARED ContextMTL queue
```

Unparking happens in `ContextMTL::FlushTasksAwaitingGPU()`, which is only invoked from the observer callback on the context's switch, it re-checks that switch before running each task:

```cpp
// impeller/renderer/backend/metal/context_mtl.mm
for (const auto& task : tasks_awaiting_gpu) {
  is_gpu_disabled_sync_switch_->Execute(fml::SyncSwitch::Handlers()
                                            .SetIfFalse([&] { task.task(); })
                                            .SetIfTrue([&] {
                                              tasks_to_queue.push_back(task);
                                            }));
}
```

TL;DR: a queue filled by all engines is drained solely according to one engine's state.

## Why didn't we notice this before?

App backgrounding is process-level: every engine observes `UIApplicationDidEnterBackground` / `WillEnterForeground` with `object:nil` and reads `UIApplication.applicationState`, so all switches flip together including, obviously, the context-owning engine. The observer fires, and everything works. That said this is basically a coincidence, not something that we enforce anywhere in code.

## Reproduction of the underlying state

`FlutterEngineGroup` stores engines in a **weak** `NSPointerArray` and spawns from
`pointerAtIndex:0` after compaction, so "create A, create B, release A, create C" will create the context with engine A, then pass that context on to B. After A is dealloc'ed, creating C will inherit the shared context (which no longer has a Shell owner) from B.

## Expected failure modes

Once the observed switch is orphaned, its value ends up frozen forever in whatever state it held when its shell was destroyed:

| Frozen value | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `false` (engine released while foregrounded) | On background, surviving engines park snapshot tasks on the shared queue. No observer ever fires. Tasks accumulate to `kMaxTasksAwaitingGPU` (1024), then the oldest are evicted and their **failure** callbacks run — `callback(nullptr)`, i.e. null snapshots. `DrainPendingImageUploads()` also never runs on suspend. |
| `true` (engine released while backgrounded) | On foreground, surviving engines resume, but any task parked on the shared queue is re-checked against the frozen switch, reads "disabled", and is **re-queued indefinitely**. |

The user-visible symptom would be `Scene.toImage` / `Picture.toImage` returning null in multi-engine apps after the first engine is released, plus a missed image-upload drain on suspend.

There's a separate case to consider too: in an **app extension** there is no `UIApplication`, so each engine derives GPU state from its own view controller's scene (`self.viewController.viewIfLoaded.window.windowScene`) and we leave it unmodified when the view controller isn't mounted in the view hierarchy. That leads to another way in which engines in a group can then hold different values while sharing one context.

## Affected apps

- **iOS only** (or more specifically, **Impeller/Metal only.**). The Skia snapshot path
  (`snapshot_controller_skia.cc`) reads the shell's switch directly and does no context-level
  parking.
- Requires `FlutterEngineGroup` / `spawnWithEntrypoint:`. Single-engine apps are unaffected: one
  shell, one switch, one context, so reader and observer are the same object.

## Potential fix ideas

1. **Give the context its own switch.** Since `ContextMTL` is shared, its notion of GPU availability should be shared too — e.g. `FlutterEngineGroup` (or the `IOSContext`) owns one switch that all member engines drive, rather than the context relying on the first engine's.
2. **Re-bind on owner death.** Have the `IOSContext` observe whichever member shell is currently alive. This is more stateful so probably worse.
3. **Aggregate the state.** The context treats the GPU as unavailable if *any* member engine says so. In theory with ensures we never submit while backgrounded, but needs some kind of multi-switch abstraction.

Of these option 1 _seems_ like it's probably the simplest but I haven't played around with this yet.

issues.body:
### RFC Pull Request Link

https://github.com/flutter/rfc/pull/21

### What problem are you solving?

Proposes updating [the official 1P plugin language policy](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/docs/ecosystem/contributing/README.md#languages) to make Kotlin the preferred language for the implementation of plugins in the flutter/packages repository. This is a follow-up to [the 2021 design document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ok_mUPgmw8_l-ynLueEKtXm2Fs48lEVB0JqZd7M7uyA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.pub7jnop54q0) which was never adopted, incorporating developments since that proposal.

issues.title: Android: multiple `--filesystem-root` values are not split by the Flutter Gradle Plugin
issues.body:
### Summary

The Flutter Gradle Plugin does not split the `filesystem-roots` Gradle property, so
`flutter build apk --filesystem-root=a --filesystem-root=b` passes the single string
`a|b` to `flutter assemble` instead of two separate roots.

### Producer

`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/android/gradle.dart` joins the roots with `|`:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/android/gradle.dart#L626

```dart
options.add('-Pfilesystem-roots=${buildInfo.fileSystemRoots.join('|')}');
```

### Consumer

`packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterCompileOptions.kt` splits on the
two-character string `\|`:

```kotlin
private const val FILE_SYSTEM_ROOTS_SEPARATOR = "\\|"

project
    .findProperty(FILE_SYSTEM_ROOTS_PROPERTY)
    ?.toString()
    ?.split(FILE_SYSTEM_ROOTS_SEPARATOR)
```

Kotlin's `String.split(vararg delimiters: String)` treats each delimiter as a literal.
The literal `\|` never appears in the joined value, so the list always has exactly one
element, and `BaseFlutterTask.fileSystemRoots` receives `["a|b"]`.

### Why this is a regression

The Groovy implementation used the same escaped source text, but Groovy's
`String.split(String)` delegates to `java.lang.String.split`, which treats the argument
as a regular expression. In Groovy, `\|` is the escaped alternation metacharacter and the
split worked.

Groovy, before the conversion:

```groovy
String[] fileSystemRootsValue = null
final String propFileSystemRoots = "filesystem-roots"
if (project.hasProperty(propFileSystemRoots)) {
    fileSystemRootsValue = project.property(propFileSystemRoots).split("\\|")
}
```

The source text carried over to Kotlin unchanged, but the semantics did not.

Regression introduced in:
- https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/166114 (reverted by https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/166666)
- https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/166676 (reland, commit 56e11aed713984b94b277d0bccd4711ee027ee63)

### Impact

`--filesystem-root` and `--filesystem-scheme` support custom source roots, used by
build systems that map Dart sources into a virtual filesystem scheme. Any Android build
that passes more than one root gets a single malformed root. A build that passes exactly
one root is unaffected.

### Fix

Change the delimiter to the literal `|`:

```kotlin
private const val FILE_SYSTEM_ROOTS_SEPARATOR = "|"
```

A unit test in
`packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/test/kotlin/FlutterCompileOptionsTest.kt` should assert
that `-Pfilesystem-roots=root1|root2` produces `listOf("root1", "root2")`. The test
coverage that existed at the time of the conversion stubbed a two-root value but never
asserted the parsed result, which is why the change passed review.

### Context

Found while reviewing https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/192488, which moves this
property parsing into `FlutterCompileOptions`. That PR preserves the behavior rather than
changing it, and leaves a `TODO` pointing at this issue.

`--filesystem-root` and `--filesystem-scheme` support custom source roots, used by
build systems that map Dart sources into a virtual filesystem scheme. Any Android build
that passes more than one root gets a single malformed root. A build that passes exactly
one root is unaffected.

### Fix

Change the delimiter to the literal `|`:

```kotlin
private const val FILE_SYSTEM_ROOTS_SEPARATOR = "|"
```

A unit test in
`packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/test/kotlin/FlutterCompileOptionsTest.kt` should assert
that `-Pfilesystem-roots=root1|root2` produces `listOf("root1", "root2")`. The test
coverage that existed at the time of the conversion stubbed a two-root value but never
asserted the parsed result, which is why the change passed review.

### Context

Found while reviewing  which moves this
property parsing into `FlutterCompileOptions`. That PR preserves the behavior rather than
changing it, and leaves a `TODO` pointing at this issue.

issues.title: [iOS 27] SystemChrome cannot show a hidden status bar with UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance=false
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Flutter iOS app.
2. Set these entries in the application's `Info.plist`:

```xml
<key>UIStatusBarHidden</key>
<true/>
<key>UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance</key>
<false/>
```

3. Build with Xcode 27 / the iOS 27 SDK and run on an iOS 27 iPhone simulator.
4. Call `SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.edgeToEdge)`, including after `SystemUiMode.immersive`.

### Expected results

`edgeToEdge` shows the status bar, and switching between `immersive` and `edgeToEdge` hides and shows it.

### Actual results

The status bar remains hidden. Changing only `UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance` to `true` and rebuilding restores both hide and show operations.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  runApp(const MaterialApp(
    home: Scaffold(
      backgroundColor: Colors.orange,
      body: Center(child: Text('iOS 27 status bar reproduction')),
    ),
  ));
  await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 3));
  await SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.edgeToEdge);
  await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 2));
  await SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.immersive);
  await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(seconds: 2));
  await SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.edgeToEdge);
}
```

### Verification

Reproduced using Flutter 3.44.8 and current master (`956e0e2469`), Xcode 27 RC (27A266a), iOS 27 simulator (24A434), and an iPhone 18 Pro simulator. `windowScene.statusBarManager.isStatusBarHidden` was sampled after each operation settled; screenshots agree with the values below.

| Operation | plist `false` | plist `true` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial Flutter view | hidden | visible |
| `edgeToEdge` | hidden | visible |
| `immersive` | hidden | hidden |
| `edgeToEdge` again | hidden | visible |

The iOS 27 SDK's `UIKit/UIApplication.h` explicitly states that setting `statusBarHidden` does nothing for applications linked against SDK versions 27.0 or later. Flutter's `FlutterPlatformPlugin` still chooses this setter when the plist value is false.

A separate minimal UIKit app confirmed that simply changing Flutter to call `prefersStatusBarHidden` / `setNeedsStatusBarAppearanceUpdate` would not fix this configuration: UIKit also ignores the view controller preference while the plist value is false. With the plist value true, the view controller path works.

Related to #128730, which tracks the deprecated UIApplication status-bar APIs more broadly. This report concerns the loss of status-bar visibility control when building an existing opt-out configuration with the iOS 27 SDK.

### Workaround

Set `UIViewControllerBasedStatusBarAppearance` to `true` (or remove the key, whose default is true), then rebuild the application. The test above retained `UIStatusBarHidden=true`; it did not require changing Dart code or the engine.

### Flutter Doctor output (relevant sections; local paths and device identifiers omitted)

issues.title: Table: width of a colSpan cell is attributed entirely to the column it starts in
issues.body:
Follow-up to #177102 (`colSpan` / `rowSpan` support in `TableCell`), tracking the `TODO(hm21)` on `RenderTable.computeMinIntrinsicWidth` in `packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/table.dart`. Filed as requested in https://github.com/flutter/flutter/commit/3064d63c5d3a5ae847ba528c932b39742b9be614#commitcomment-200409272. Related: #21594.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out the branch of #177102.
2. Build a `Table` with `IntrinsicColumnWidth` columns in which a `TableCell(colSpan: 2)` sits above two narrower cells (code sample below).
3. Wrap it in `IntrinsicWidth` (or read `getMinIntrinsicWidth` / `getMaxIntrinsicWidth` on the `RenderTable`).

### Expected results

The table is 300 wide. The spanning cell needs 300 across both columns, and the two 50-wide cells in the second row fit in any split of that (for example 250 + 50 or 150 + 150).

### Actual results

The table is 350 wide; `getMinIntrinsicWidth` and `getMaxIntrinsicWidth` also report 350. Column 0 is sized to 300 for the spanning cell and column 1 to 50 for its own cell.

`RenderTable` sizes its columns one at a time: `_computeColumnWidths`, `computeMinIntrinsicWidth` and `computeMaxIntrinsicWidth` hand `TableColumnWidth.minIntrinsicWidth` / `maxIntrinsicWidth` the cells of a single column (`column(x)`). A cell with `colSpan > 1` is part of the column it starts in, so its whole width is attributed to that one column instead of being shared between the columns it covers.

Sharing it means growing only the columns whose width actually depends on their cells. A `FixedColumnWidth` (or `FractionColumnWidth`) column has to keep the width it asked for, and `TableColumnWidth` currently does not expose whether it is cell-driven, so `RenderTable` cannot tell which columns of a span may absorb the extra width. A fix probably needs a small addition to the `TableColumnWidth` API first.

The test `colSpan attributes the cell width to the column it starts in` in `packages/flutter/test/rendering/table_test.dart` pins the current behaviour and should be updated with the fix.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

void main() {
  runApp(
    Directionality(
      textDirection: TextDirection.ltr,
      child: Center(
        child: IntrinsicWidth(
          child: Table(
            defaultColumnWidth: const IntrinsicColumnWidth(),
            children: const <TableRow>[
              TableRow(
                children: <Widget>[
                  TableCell(colSpan: 2, child: SizedBox(width: 300, height: 20)),
                  TableCell.none,
                ],
              ),
              TableRow(
                children: <Widget>[
                  SizedBox(width: 50, height: 20),
                  SizedBox(width: 50, height: 20),
                ],
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    ),
  );
}
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

Framework at flutter/flutter@3064d63c5d3a5ae847ba528c932b39742b9be614 (branch of #177102, based on master 0b1bac2ff48). Not reproducible on master yet, since `colSpan` only exists on that branch.

[Android] Engine never calls `EdgeToEdge.enable()`, so Play Console's "Edge-to-edge may not display for all users" persists after #165328
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a release app bundle of any Flutter app targeting SDK 35+ with Flutter 3.47.x (`flutter build appbundle --release`).
2. Upload it to a Google Play track and open the release's **App quality / release insights** panel in Play Console.

The app in question calls `SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.edgeToEdge)` at startup and handles every inset in the widget tree (status bar, navigation bar, display cutouts, keyboard), so the warning is not about an app-side inset bug.

### Expected results

No `Edge-to-edge may not display for all users` warning, since https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/165328 ("Use `EdgeToEdge.enableEdgeToEdge` to set edge-to-edge mode instead of `View` flags") is closed as completed, and the PR that closed it, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/183072, described this in its summary:

> - For `ComponentActivity` instances (e.g. `FlutterFragmentActivity`), uses `EdgeToEdge.enable()` **which also suppresses Android 15 edge-to-edge warnings**
> - For plain `Activity` instances (e.g. `FlutterActivity`), falls back to `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows()` which achieves the same layout behavior

### Actual results

Play Console still shows:

> **Edge-to-edge may not display for all users**
> From Android 15, apps targeting SDK 35 will display edge-to-edge by default. Apps targeting SDK 35 should handle insets to make sure that their app displays correctly on Android 15 and later. Investigate this issue and allow time to test edge-to-edge and make the required updates. Alternatively, call `enableEdgeToEdge()` for Kotlin or `EdgeToEdge.enable()` for Java for backward compatibility.

The `ComponentActivity` branch described in #183072's summary is not in the merged code. The merged commit 6093dca2 only ever calls `WindowCompat`, and that is still true on `main` today:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9ead586c1e139a8464d70b6cdf07d475aab99808/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/plugin/platform/PlatformPlugin.java#L458-L464

```java
  private void enableEdgeToEdge() {
    // Clear previously applied system UI visibility flags to ensure that
    // WindowInsetsControllerCompat can correctly configure the window.
    activity.getWindow().getDecorView().setSystemUiVisibility(0);

    WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(activity.getWindow(), false);
  }
```

A code search for `EdgeToEdge` under `engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android` returns only `PlatformChannel.java`, `PlatformPlugin.java` and `PlatformPluginTest.java`, all of which are the `SystemUiMode.EDGE_TO_EDGE` enum and the private method above. `androidx.activity.EdgeToEdge` is never referenced anywhere in the Android embedding.

Play Console's check is a static scan of the app's bytecode for an `enableEdgeToEdge()` / `EdgeToEdge.enable()` call site; `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)` does not satisfy it. So no amount of correct inset handling on the Flutter side clears the warning, and there is nothing an app author can do from Dart.

Working around it in app code is also not straightforward: `enableEdgeToEdge()` is an extension on `androidx.activity.ComponentActivity`, and `FlutterActivity` extends plain `android.app.Activity`:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/9ead586c1e139a8464d70b6cdf07d475aab99808/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/android/FlutterActivity.java#L211-L212

```java
public class FlutterActivity extends Activity
    implements FlutterActivityAndFragmentDelegate.Host, LifecycleOwner {
```

So the only app-side workaround is to migrate the host to `FlutterFragmentActivity` purely to satisfy a static analyzer, which is a real behavioral change (fragment hosting, cached engine) for a cosmetic warning. Plugins that ship their own `FlutterActivity` subclass make that migration harder still.

### Why this is worth reopening rather than another duplicate

#169810, #175262, #183372, #184350 and #184351 were all closed as duplicates of #165328, with the reasoning that the migration would resolve the Play Console warnings once it landed. #165328 is now closed as completed, but the part of the migration that actually addressed the warning (`EdgeToEdge.enable()` for `ComponentActivity` hosts) did not ship, so the warning persists on current stable with no remaining tracking issue.

### Proposal

Restore the `ComponentActivity` branch from #183072's summary: when `activity instanceof ComponentActivity`, call `EdgeToEdge.enable()` and keep the `WindowCompat` fallback for plain `Activity` hosts. Making `FlutterActivity` itself a `ComponentActivity` would cover every host, but that is a larger change.


[tool_crash] StateError (Bad state: No element) in testCompilerBuildNativeAssets
issues.body:
### Description

In Flutter 3.47.3 crash telemetry, `testCompilerBuildNativeAssets` threw an unhandled `StateError: Bad state: No element` (36 crashes in the first 7 days post-release).

### Stack Trace

```text
Iterable.firstWhere at dart:core/iterable.dart:722
testCompilerBuildNativeAssets at package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/test/native_assets.dart:37
TestCompilerNativeAssetsBuilderImpl.build at package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/test/native_assets.dart:22
TestCommand.runCommand at package:flutter_tools/src/commands/test.dart:504
```

### Cause

In `package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/test/native_assets.dart`:
```dart
final Uri projectUri = FlutterProject.current().directory.uri;
final String runPackageName = buildInfo.packageConfig.packages
    .firstWhere((Package p) => p.root == projectUri)
    .name;
```
`firstWhere` throws `StateError` when no package in `buildInfo.packageConfig.packages` has its `root` matching `projectUri` (for example, in pub workspaces, symlinked directories, or when invoking `flutter test` from a sub-directory).

### Proposed Fix

Use `firstWhereOrNull` or check against root URIs and fall back gracefully to the target project/package name from pubspec rather than crashing.

[tool_crash] SocketException (Error event raised in event handler : error condition has been reset, port = 0) in _NativeSocket.multiplex
issues.body:
### Description

In Flutter 3.47.3 crash telemetry, low-level socket reset errors on Linux caused unhandled `SocketException` crashes (27 crashes in the first 7 days post-release).

### Stack Trace

```text
_NativeSocket.multiplex at dart:io-patch/socket_patch.dart:1767
_RawReceivePort._handleMessage at dart:isolate-patch/isolate_patch.dart:192
```

Error message:
```text
SocketException: Error event raised in event handler : error condition has been reset, port = 0
```

### Cause

During resident runner, daemon, or recompile socket multiplexing on Linux, a socket reset event (`ECONNRESET` or similar) handled in `_NativeSocket.multiplex` raises an unhandled error into the Dart Zone if the enclosing stream or socket controller is not guarding error events.

### Proposed Fix

Investigate socket error listeners across the resident runner and VM service connection to ensure socket reset error events on Linux are caught and handled cleanly.

issues.title: [webview_flutter_wkwebview] iOS unowned registrar abort in late script messages and codec encoding after teardown
issues.body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

webview_flutter (iOS implementation: webview_flutter_wkwebview)

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

No. The deterministic reproduction uses unchanged released webview_flutter_wkwebview 3.25.1 sources. This report does not claim a reproduction on the latest published version.

### Dependency versions

```yaml
webview_flutter: 4.13.1
webview_flutter_wkwebview: 3.25.1
webview_flutter_platform_interface: 2.15.1
```

### Summary

Two native Swift lifetime failures occur after ProxyAPIRegistrar teardown:

1. A retained ScriptMessageHandlerImpl receives a late WebKit message and dereferences its unowned registrar.
2. A retained FlutterStandardMessageCodec encodes a value and its WebKitLibraryPigeonInternalProxyApiCodecReaderWriter dereferences its unowned registrar.

Both abort with `Fatal error: Attempted to read an unowned reference but object ... was already destroyed`.

Related: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/168535 (termination/deallocation) and https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/170643 (a different hot-restart/channel failure). This report supplies a deterministic native lifetime reproduction for the two paths above. Please merge into the existing report if maintainers consider it the same underlying bug.

### Steps to reproduce

This is a native mechanism reproduction, not a claim that ordinary Flutter navigation/backgrounding alone deterministically triggers the crash.

1. Obtain the unchanged native Swift sources from the released 3.25.1 package: `darwin/webview_flutter_wkwebview/Sources/webview_flutter_wkwebview/*.swift`.
2. Copy those sources into a scratch directory's `Sources/` subdirectory. Save the two Swift files below alongside it.
3. Boot an arm64 iOS simulator. Set `FLUTTER_FRAMEWORK_DIR` to the simulator slice of the Flutter SDK's cached `Flutter.xcframework`.
4. Build and run the harness using the commands below, once with `handler` and once with `codec` (each aborts its process).
5. The harness retains a handler and codec, calls the plugin's actual applicationWillTerminate teardown hook, drains an autorelease pool, and confirms registrar deallocation through a weak reference before invoking the late operation.

```sh
export FLUTTER_FRAMEWORK_DIR="/path/to/flutter/bin/cache/artifacts/engine/ios/Flutter.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
xcrun swiftc -target arm64-apple-ios18.0-simulator \
  -sdk "$(xcrun --sdk iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path)" \
  -F "$FLUTTER_FRAMEWORK_DIR" -framework Flutter -framework WebKit -framework UIKit \
  -o repro Sources/*.swift TestBinaryMessenger.swift main.swift
SIMCTL_CHILD_DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH="$FLUTTER_FRAMEWORK_DIR" xcrun simctl spawn booted "$PWD/repro" handler
SIMCTL_CHILD_DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH="$FLUTTER_FRAMEWORK_DIR" xcrun simctl spawn booted "$PWD/repro" codec
```

No network content or app backends are required. `encode(nil)` does not reproduce the writer path; `encode("test")` does.

### Expected results

Late native callbacks and outstanding codec/reply work should not dereference a deallocated registrar. Teardown should safely cancel/ignore work or maintain ownership for the remaining operation.

### Actual results

Both modes terminate with SIGABRT. Symbolized simulator crash reports identify the same failing native functions as production reports.

### Code sample

`main.swift`:

```swift
import Flutter
import WebKit
import UIKit
weak var weakRegistrar: ProxyAPIRegistrar?
let (plugin,codec,handler) = autoreleasepool { () -> (WebViewFlutterPlugin,FlutterStandardMessageCodec,WKScriptMessageHandler) in
 let plugin = WebViewFlutterPlugin(binaryMessenger: TestBinaryMessenger())
 weakRegistrar = plugin.proxyApiRegistrar!
 let codec = plugin.proxyApiRegistrar!.codec
 let api = plugin.proxyApiRegistrar!.apiDelegate.pigeonApiWKScriptMessageHandler(plugin.proxyApiRegistrar!)
 let handler = try! api.pigeonDelegate.pigeonDefaultConstructor(pigeonApi: api)
 return (plugin,codec,handler)
}
print("REPRO_READY mode=\(CommandLine.arguments.last!)")
autoreleasepool { plugin.applicationWillTerminate(UIApplication.shared) }
print("REGISTRAR_DEALLOCATED \(weakRegistrar == nil)")
if CommandLine.arguments.last == "codec" { _ = codec.encode("test") }
else { handler.userContentController(WKUserContentController(), didReceive: WKScriptMessage()) }
print("REPRO_SURVIVED")
```

`TestBinaryMessenger.swift` (the package's test messenger; preserves the real plugin/codec/native handler implementations):

```swift
// Copyright 2013 The Flutter Authors
// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style license that can be
// found in the LICENSE file.

#if os(iOS)
  import Flutter
#elseif os(macOS)
  import FlutterMacOS
#else
  #error("Unsupported platform.")
#endif

class TestBinaryMessenger: NSObject, FlutterBinaryMessenger {
  func send(onChannel channel: String, message: Data?) {

  }

  func send(
    onChannel channel: String, message: Data?, binaryReply callback: FlutterBinaryReply? = nil
  ) {

  }

  func setMessageHandlerOnChannel(
    _ channel: String, binaryMessageHandler handler: FlutterBinaryMessageHandler? = nil
  ) -> FlutterBinaryMessengerConnection {
    return 0
  }

  func cleanUpConnection(_ connection: FlutterBinaryMessengerConnection) {

  }
}
```

### Logs

Handler reproduction:

```text
REPRO_READY mode=handler
REGISTRAR_DEALLOCATED true
Fatal error: Attempted to read an unowned reference but object ... was already destroyed
Child process terminated with signal 6: Abort trap

Symbolized failing frames:
swift_unownedRetainStrong
ScriptMessageHandlerImpl.userContentController(_:didReceive:)
```

Codec reproduction:

```text
REPRO_READY mode=codec
REGISTRAR_DEALLOCATED true
Fatal error: Attempted to read an unowned reference but object ... was already destroyed
Child process terminated with signal 6: Abort trap

Symbolized failing frames:
swift_unownedRetainStrong
WebKitLibraryPigeonInternalProxyApiCodecReaderWriter.writer(with:)
-[FlutterStandardMessageCodec encode:]
```

Sanitized production evidence from Firebase Crashlytics:

- Reviewed five recent events for each signature (ten total); all ten reported the app in the background, across multiple unrelated WebView screens.
- Events occur both during loading and after the WebView is visible, on several iPhone models.
- In all five codec events, the stack shows a WebViewProxyAPIDelegate.evaluateJavaScript completion, a generated Pigeon reply, FlutterBasicMessageChannel reply handling, FlutterStandardMessageCodec encoding, and the codec writer's unowned-reference abort.
- The other five events fail in ScriptMessageHandlerImpl.userContentController(_:didReceive:).
- One event includes memory-pressure context; that is not universal.
- These reports do not identify whether application termination, scene disconnection, or engine detachment destroyed the registrar in production. Background state alone is not proof of engine teardown.

### Investigation / regression-test suggestions

An isolated weak-reference/guard change in ScriptMessageHandlerImpl prevents the handler harness abort but leaves the codec harness abort unchanged. Therefore, guarding only incoming script messages does not address both paths.

Please cover late incoming script messages and pending evaluateJavaScript reply serialization during registrar teardown, including lifetime of generated codec helpers. Any ownership fix should also be checked for retain cycles and messaging after engine shutdown. We have not validated a complete production patch.

### Flutter Doctor output / reproduction environment

The native harness was compiled and executed with:

```text
Flutter 3.44.3, stable
Framework revision e1fd963c6f
Engine revision a4ce257c68
Dart 3.12.2
Xcode 26.6 (17F113)
arm64 iOS Simulator: iPhone 17, iOS 26.4
webview_flutter_wkwebview native sources: released 3.25.1, unchanged
```

The harness uses the real Flutter.framework, UIKit and WebKit; only the binary messenger is a test double. It deliberately delivers the operation after teardown, so it establishes the lifetime defect rather than reproducing the complete production user journey.
